title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
湖廣鄉試錄序
聖天子丕承
駿命于兹十有七年天下以鄉
舉選士凡五科矣成化庚子
復當大比之期湖廣藩臬重
臣援故事預聘元等以司去
留時太監王定韋貴以鎮南
===
服惇崇儒雅都察院右副都
御史白行順大理寺右少卿
吳道宏受
命宣撫咸汲汲作興士類巡按監
察御史楊謐寔総試事以興
賢
國家令典尤究心焉提調學校
punctuated:
湖廣鄉試錄序

聖天子丕承駿命，于兹十有七年，天下以鄉舉選士凡五科矣。成化庚子，復當大比之期，湖廣藩臬重臣援故事，預聘元等以司去留。時太監王定、韋貴以鎮南服，惇崇儒雅；都察院右副都御史白行順、大理寺右少卿吳道宏受命宣撫，咸汲汲作興士類。巡按監察御史楊謐寔総試事，以興賢，國家令典，尤究心焉。提調學校
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Huguang Provincial Examination

The sagely Son of Heaven has grandly inherited Heaven’s great mandate. In these seventeen years, five rounds of examinations have been held throughout the realm to select scholars through provincial recommendation. In the gengzi year of Chenghua [1480], the time for the triennial examination came around again. Following precedent, the senior officials of Huguang’s Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions engaged Yuan and the others in advance to determine which candidates should pass and which should be rejected.

At that time, the eunuch directors Wang Ding and Wei Gui, stationed to guard the southern region, earnestly honored Confucian learning and refinement. Bai Xingshun, Right Vice Censor-in-chief of the Censorate, and Wu Daohong, Right Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review, had received orders to conduct a mission of pacification. All were eager to encourage and foster the scholars. Yang Mi, the Regional Inspector serving as an Investigating Censor, was in overall charge of the examination. title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
副使薛綱先期徧歷郡邑考
其可舉者得千三百有竒俾
就試有司至期環棘三試之
提調則左布政使何喬新左
參議徐恪監試則副使徐懷
僉事汪進贊理防範則左參
政倪輔右參政馮孜副使馬
===
震武清王億右參議楊琚林
迪韓文僉事蕭禎李冕萬繡
徐輝龔澤郭經姚倫曁百執
事懋簡以充咸矢厥心愼厥
事罔敢怠遑既撤棘取其文
之合於經者得八十五人遵
制額也迺次其氏名并錄文之

He selected more than thirteen hundred and directed them to sit the examination before the responsible authorities. Serving as Proctors were Left Provincial Administration Commissioner He Qiaoxin and Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Xu Ke; overseeing the examination were Surveillance Vice Commissioner Xu Huai and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Wang Jin. Assisting with arrangements and security were Left Administration Vice Commissioner Ni Fu; Right Administration Vice Commissioner Feng Zi; Surveillance Vice Commissioners Ma Zhen, Wu Qing, and Wang Yi; Right Assistant Administration Commissioners Yang Ju, Lin Di, and Han Wen; and Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Xiao Zhen, Li Mian, Wan Xiu, Xu Hui, Gong Ze, Guo Jing, and Yao Lun. title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
粹者為鄉試錄以獻于
朝僉謂元宜有序仰惟我
太祖高皇帝肇造區夏當天下甫
定之初即詔有司以科目取
士凡規畫皆斷自
聖心又嘗諭吏部曰鴻鵠之能遠
舉者為其有羽翼也蛟龍之
===
能騰躍者為其有鱗鬣也人
君之能致治者為其有賢人
以為之輔也大哉
皇言所以開億萬載太平之業者
在是矣
聖子神孫祗遹
彝典繇是賢才出為
punctuated: 粹者為鄉試錄，以獻于朝。僉謂元宜有序。仰惟我太祖高皇帝肇造區夏，當天下甫定之初，即詔有司以科目取士，凡規畫皆斷自聖心。又嘗諭吏部曰：「鴻鵠之能遠舉者，為其有羽翼也；蛟龍之能騰躍者，為其有鱗鬣也；人君之能致治者，為其有賢人以為之輔也。」大哉，皇言！所以開億萬載太平之業者，在是矣。聖子神孫祗遹彝典，繇是賢才出為
translation_en: …the finest among them into a Record of the Provincial Examination, to be presented to the court. All agreed that Yuan should supply a preface. Reverently considering how our Emperor Taizu Gao founded the realm, we recall that, just as All under Heaven had first been pacified, he commanded the responsible officials to select men through the civil-service examinations. Every arrangement was decided by his sagely mind. He also once instructed the Ministry of Personnel: “Wild geese and swans can fly far because they have wings; dragons can soar and leap because they have scales and manes; a ruler can achieve good government because he has worthy men to assist him.” Great indeed are these imperial words! Herein lies the means of establishing an enduring foundation of peace for countless ages. His sagely sons and divine grandsons have reverently followed these established statutes. Thus worthy and talented men have come forth to serve…

title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
國家之用者彬彬焉湖廣東南
名藩衡岳之嵽嵲江漢之泓
渟靈淑之氣鍾為俊英百餘
年来士繇科目進者或以文
學魁天下或以謀猷賛
聖謨或以宏材懿德宣力乎四方
於戲盛哉昔先正有言豪傑
===
之士繇科目而進誠哉是言
也夫
國家以科目取士以豪傑之士
待之也諸士子登名賢書行
将試禮闈奉
廷對顯融于時盍以豪傑之士
自待乎道德足以經邦文章
punctuated: 國家之用者彬彬焉。湖廣，東南名藩，衡岳之嵽嵲，江漢之泓渟，靈淑之氣鍾為俊英。百餘年来，士繇科目進者，或以文學魁天下，或以謀猷賛聖謨，或以宏材懿德宣力乎四方。於戲，盛哉！昔先正有言：「豪傑之士繇科目而進。」誠哉，是言也！夫國家以科目取士，以豪傑之士待之也。諸士子登名賢書，行将試禮闈，奉廷對，顯融于時，盍以豪傑之士自待乎？道德足以經邦，文章
translation_en: …for service to the state are abundant in their cultivated excellence. Huguang is a renowned province of the southeast. From the towering heights of Mount Heng and the deep, still waters of the Yangzi and Han rivers, numinous and auspicious influences gather to produce outstanding men. For more than a hundred years, men who have advanced through the examinations have variously led the realm in literary learning, assisted the imperial plans with their counsel, or devoted their great talents and admirable virtue to service throughout the land. Ah, how flourishing! A worthy predecessor once said, “Men of exceptional ability advance through the examinations.” How true these words are! The state selects men through the examinations and expects them to be men of exceptional ability. You candidates whose names have been entered on the roll of worthies will soon sit the Metropolitan Examination, respectfully present your answers at the Palace Examination, and attain distinction in your age. Should you not hold yourselves to the standards of men of exceptional ability? Your moral cultivation should suffice to govern the realm, and your literary accomplishments…

title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
足以華國風節足以厲俗以
為
聖世之羽翼鱗鬣斯可謂豪傑之
士而無負
朝廷期待之德意矣不然影纓
鳴珮而德與業無聞焉是科
目之玷也是鄉郡之羞也是
===
元與二三執事者之辱也豈
不有負
列聖興賢之令典哉庸序諸卷首
以為多士勗
廣東廣州府東莞縣儒學教
諭李元謹序
punctuated:
足以華國，風節足以厲俗，以為聖世之羽翼鱗鬣，斯可謂豪傑之士，而無負朝廷期待之德意矣。不然，影纓鳴珮，而德與業無聞焉，是科目之玷也，是鄉郡之羞也，是元與二三執事者之辱也，豈不有負列聖興賢之令典哉？庸序諸卷首，以為多士勗。
廣東廣州府東莞縣儒學教諭李元謹序。
translation_en:
…sufficient to adorn the realm, and integrity sufficient to elevate prevailing customs, thereby serving as wings and feathers, scales and fins, to this sage age: such men may indeed be called outstanding scholars, worthy of the gracious expectations the court has placed upon them. Otherwise, if they merely display their cap tassels [?] and make their jade pendants chime, while their virtue and accomplishments remain unheard of, they disgrace the examination system, shame their home districts and prefectures, and bring dishonor upon me, Yuan, and my fellow officials engaged in this undertaking. Would this not betray the excellent institutions established by successive sage emperors to advance worthy men? I therefore set this preface at the beginning of the volume to encourage the assembled scholars.
Preface respectfully composed by Li Yuan, Instructor of the Confucian School of Dongguan County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong.

title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
瑟兮僩兮者恂慄也赫兮喧兮者威儀也
師冕見及階子曰階也及席子曰席也皆
坐子告之曰某在斯某在斯師冕出子
張問曰與師言之道與子曰然固相師
之道也
陳良楚產也悅周公仲尼之道北學於中
國北方之學者未能或之先也彼所謂
===
豪傑之士也
易
飛龍在天乃位乎天德
九四噬乾胏得金矢利艱貞吉象曰利艱
貞吉未光也六五噬乾肉得黃金貞厲
无咎象曰貞厲无咎得當也
知周乎萬物而道濟天下故不過旁行而
不流樂天知命故不憂安土敦乎仁故
能愛
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

瑟兮僩兮者，恂慄也；赫兮喧兮者，威儀也。

師冕見，及階，子曰：「階也。」及席，子曰：「席也。」皆坐，子告之曰：「某在斯，某在斯。」師冕出，子張問曰：「與師言之道與？」子曰：「然，固相師之道也。」

陳良，楚產也，悅周公、仲尼之道，北學於中國。北方之學者，未能或之先也。彼所謂豪傑之士也。

易

飛龍在天，乃位乎天德。

九四，噬乾胏，得金矢，利艱貞，吉。象曰：「利艱貞，吉」，未光也。六五，噬乾肉，得黃金，貞厲，无咎。象曰：「貞厲，无咎」，得當也。

知周乎萬物，而道濟天下，故不過；旁行而不流，樂天知命，故不憂；安土敦乎仁，故能愛。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“Grave and dignified” signifies reverent apprehension; “illustrious and imposing” signifies an awe-inspiring bearing.

Music Master Mian came to see Confucius. When he reached the steps, the Master said, “Here are the steps.” When he reached the mat, the Master said, “Here is the mat.” Once everyone was seated, the Master told him, “So-and-so is here; so-and-so is here.” After Music Master Mian left, Zizhang asked, “Is this the way to speak to a music master?” The Master said, “Yes. This is indeed the way to assist a music master.”

Chen Liang was a native of Chu. Delighting in the Way of the Duke of Zhou and Zhongni [Confucius], he went north to study in the Central States. None of the scholars of the north could surpass him. He was what is called a man of outstanding talent.

Book of Changes

“A flying dragon in heaven”: he thus occupies a position endowed with heavenly virtue.

Nine in the fourth place: Biting through dried meat on the bone, one obtains a metal arrow. It is beneficial to remain steadfast amid difficulty. Auspicious. The Image says: “It is beneficial to remain steadfast amid difficulty. Auspicious”—because the light is not yet brilliant. Six in the fifth place: Biting through dried meat, one obtains yellow gold. Remaining steadfast amid danger, one incurs no blame. The Image says: “Remaining steadfast amid danger, one incurs no blame”—because one has attained the appropriate position.

His wisdom encompasses the myriad things, and his Way brings aid to all under heaven; therefore he does not err. He moves in all directions without being swept astray. He delights in Heaven and understands its mandate; therefore he does not worry. He rests content where he dwells and is steadfast in benevolence; therefore he is able to love.

title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
定其交而後求
書
乃聖乃神乃武乃文
予念我先神后之勞爾先予丕克羞爾用
懷爾然
惟天降命肇我民惟元祀
未定于宗禮亦未克敉公功迪將其後監
我士師工誕保文武受民
詩
===
一之日于貉取彼狐狸為公子裘二之日
其同載纘武功言私其豵獻豜于公五
月斯螽動股六月莎雞振羽七月在野
八月在宇九月在戶十月蟋蟀入我牀
下穹窒熏鼠塞向墐戶嗟我婦子曰為
改歲入此室處六月食鬱及薁七月亨
葵及菽八月剝棗十月穫稻為此春酒
以介眉壽七月食瓜八月斷壺九月叔
苴采荼薪樗食我農夫
punctuated:
定其交而後求。

書
乃聖乃神，乃武乃文。
予念我先神后之勞爾先，予丕克羞爾用懷爾，然。
惟天降命，肇我民惟元祀。
未定于宗禮，亦未克敉公功。迪將其後，監我士師工，誕保文武受民。

詩
一之日于貉，取彼狐狸，為公子裘。二之日其同，載纘武功。言私其豵，獻豜于公。五月斯螽動股，六月莎雞振羽。七月在野，八月在宇，九月在戶，十月蟋蟀入我牀下。穹窒熏鼠，塞向墐戶。嗟我婦子，曰為改歲，入此室處。六月食鬱及薁，七月亨葵及菽。八月剝棗，十月穫稻。為此春酒，以介眉壽。七月食瓜，八月斷壺，九月叔苴。采荼薪樗，食我農夫。
translation_en:
…Establish firm relations with others before making requests.

Book of Documents

Sagacious and wondrous, martial and cultured.

I remember how our former divine sovereigns labored for your ancestors. I shall greatly advance and employ you, thereby cherishing you: so shall it be.

Heaven bestowed its mandate; the beginning for our people was that first year of sacrifice.

…The ancestral rites have not yet been settled, nor have I yet been able to consolidate your achievements, Duke. Continue to carry them forward hereafter; oversee our officers, leaders, and functionaries, and greatly safeguard the people received by Kings Wen and Wu.

Book of Odes

In the first month, we hunt badgers, taking foxes and wildcats to make fur robes for our lord’s sons. In the second month, all assemble and continue their martial work. We keep the young boars for ourselves and present the full-grown boars to our lord.

In the fifth month, the locusts move their thighs; in the sixth month, the katydids flutter their wings. In the seventh month, the crickets are in the fields; in the eighth, beneath the eaves; in the ninth, at the door; in the tenth, they come beneath our beds. We stop up the holes and smoke out the rats, block the north-facing windows and plaster the doorways. Ah, our wives and children! The year is turning: come into this room and dwell here.

In the sixth month, we eat wild plums and wild grapes; in the seventh, we boil mallows and beans. In the eighth, we beat down the jujubes; in the tenth, we harvest rice. With it we make spring wine to secure long life. In the seventh month, we eat melons; in the eighth, we cut gourds; in the ninth, we gather hempseed. We gather bitter greens and cut ailanthus for firewood, feeding our husbandmen.

title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
允矣君子展也大成
申伯信邁王餞于郿申伯還南謝于誠歸
王命召伯徹申伯土疆以峙其粻式遄
其行申伯番番既入于謝徒御啴啴周
邦咸喜戎有良翰不顯申伯王之元舅
文武是憲
既右烈考亦右文母
春秋
夏城中丘〔隱公七年〕浚洙〔莊公九年〕冬城防〔襄公十三年〕
===
仲孫何忌會晋韓不信齊高張宋仲幾
衛世叔申鄭國參曹人莒人薛人杞人
小邾人城成周〔昭公三十二年〕
諸侯城緣陵〔僖公十四年〕仲孫羯會晋荀盈齊高
止宋華定衛世叔儀鄭公孫段曹人莒
人滕人薛人小邾人城杞〔襄公二十九年〕
公會晋侯齊侯宋公蔡侯鄭伯衛子莒子
盟于踐土 公朝于王所 公子遂如
齊〔並僖公二十八年〕齊侯使國歸父来聘〔僖公三十三年〕
punctuated:
允矣君子，展也大成。

申伯信邁，王餞于郿。申伯還南，謝于誠歸。王命召伯，徹申伯土疆，以峙其粻，式遄其行。申伯番番，既入于謝，徒御啴啴，周邦咸喜。戎有良翰，不顯申伯，王之元舅，文武是憲。

既右烈考，亦右文母。

春秋

夏，城中丘。〔隱公七年〕浚洙。〔莊公九年〕冬，城防。〔襄公十三年〕

仲孫何忌會晋韓不信、齊高張、宋仲幾、衛世叔申、鄭國參、曹人、莒人、薛人、杞人、小邾人，城成周。〔昭公三十二年〕

諸侯城緣陵。〔僖公十四年〕仲孫羯會晋荀盈、齊高止、宋華定、衛世叔儀、鄭公孫段、曹人、莒人、滕人、薛人、小邾人，城杞。〔襄公二十九年〕

公會晋侯、齊侯、宋公、蔡侯、鄭伯、衛子、莒子，盟于踐土。公朝于王所。公子遂如齊。〔並僖公二十八年〕齊侯使國歸父来聘。〔僖公三十三年〕
translation_en:
Trustworthy indeed is the noble man; truly great is his accomplishment.

The Earl of Shen set forth indeed, and the king gave him a farewell feast at Mei. The Earl of Shen returned south; to Xie he truly returned. The king commanded the Earl of Shao to delimit the Earl of Shen’s territory and lay up provisions for him, thereby hastening his journey. The Earl of Shen, stately and martial, entered Xie; his footmen and charioteers were numerous and imposing. All the realm of Zhou rejoiced: “You have a worthy supporting pillar!” How illustrious is the Earl of Shen, the king’s senior maternal uncle, who takes Kings Wen and Wu as his models!

He aided his illustrious deceased father and also aided his cultured mother.

Spring and Autumn Annals

In summer, Zhongqiu was fortified. 〔Seventh year of Duke Yin.〕 The Zhu River was dredged. 〔Ninth year of Duke Zhuang.〕 In winter, Fang was fortified. 〔Thirteenth year of Duke Xiang.〕

Zhongsun Heji met with Han Buxin of Jin, Gao Zhang of Qi, Zhong Ji of Song, Shishu Shen of Wei, Guo Can of Zheng, and men of Cao, Ju, Xue, Qi, and Lesser Zhu to fortify Chengzhou. 〔Thirty-second year of Duke Zhao.〕

The regional lords fortified Yuanling. 〔Fourteenth year of Duke Xi.〕 Zhongsun Jie met with Xun Ying of Jin, Gao Zhi of Qi, Hua Ding of Song, Shishu Yi of Wei, Gongsun Duan of Zheng, and men of Cao, Ju, Teng, Xue, and Lesser Zhu to fortify Qi. 〔Twenty-ninth year of Duke Xiang.〕

The duke met with the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, the Viscount of Wei, and the Viscount of Ju to conclude a covenant at Jiantu. The duke paid court at the king’s place of residence. The duke’s son Sui went to Qi. 〔All in the twenty-eighth year of Duke Xi.〕 The Marquis of Qi sent Guo Guifu on a diplomatic visit to our court. 〔Thirty-third year of Duke Xi.〕

title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
晋人宋人衛人曹人同盟于清丘宋
師伐陳衛人救陳〔並宣公十二年〕楚子伐宋〔宣公十三年〕
季孫行父臧孫許叔孫僑如公孫嬰齊帥
師會晋郤克衛孫良夫曹公子首及齊
侯戰于鞌齊師敗績〔成公二年〕
禮記
名子者不以國不以日月不以隱疾不以
山川
炮取豚若將刲之刳之實棗於其腹中編
===
萑以苴之塗之以謹塗炮之塗皆乾擘
之濯手以摩之去其皽為稻粉糔溲之
以為酏以付豚煎諸膏膏必滅之鉅鑊
湯以小鼎薌脯於其中使其湯毋滅鼎
三日三夜毋絕火而后調之以醯醢
宵雅肄三官其始也
東面執八筭興請賓曰順投為入比投不
釋
第貳場
punctuated:
晋人、宋人、衛人、曹人同盟于清丘。宋師伐陳，衛人救陳。〔並宣公十二年〕楚子伐宋。〔宣公十三年〕季孫行父、臧孫許、叔孫僑如、公孫嬰齊帥師，會晋郤克、衛孫良夫、曹公子首，及齊侯戰于鞌，齊師敗績。〔成公二年〕
禮記
名子者，不以國，不以日月，不以隱疾，不以山川。
炮：取豚，若將，刲之，刳之，實棗於其腹中，編萑以苴之，塗之以謹，塗炮之。塗皆乾，擘之，濯手以摩之，去其皽。為稻粉，糔溲之以為酏，以付豚，煎諸膏，膏必滅之。鉅鑊湯，以小鼎薌脯於其中，使其湯毋滅鼎。三日三夜毋絕火，而后調之以醯醢。
宵雅肄三，官其始也。
東面，執八筭，興，請賓曰：「順投為入，比投不釋。」
第貳場
translation_en:
Representatives of Jin, Song, Wei, and Cao jointly concluded a covenant at Qingqiu. The army of Song attacked Chen; representatives of Wei came to Chen’s aid. 〔Both entries concern the twelfth year of Duke Xuan.〕 The ruler of Chu attacked Song. 〔The thirteenth year of Duke Xuan.〕 Jisun Xingfu, Zangsun Xu, Shusun Qiaoru, and Gongsun Yingqi led troops to join Xi Ke of Jin, Sun Liangfu of Wei, and Prince Shou of Cao in battle against the Marquis of Qi at An. The army of Qi suffered a crushing defeat. 〔The second year of Duke Cheng.〕
Record of Rites (Liji)
In naming a son, one does not use the name of a state, the sun or moon, a concealed ailment, or mountains or rivers.
For roasting: take a piglet, or [a sheep?; the transcription is doubtful], slaughter and eviscerate it, and fill its belly with dates. Weave reeds to wrap it, coat it with clay [?], and roast it in this coating. When the coating is completely dry, break it open. Wash your hands and rub the animal, removing its outer skin. Make rice flour, moisten and mix it into a batter, and apply it to the piglet. Fry it in fat, which must cover it completely. Heat water in a large cauldron and place a small tripod vessel inside it to cook the meat [?], ensuring that the water does not submerge the small vessel. Keep the fire burning continuously for three days and three nights, then season it with vinegar and minced-meat sauce.
Have them practice the first three poems of the Lesser Odes: this provides the foundation for entering official service.
Facing east and holding eight tally rods, he rises and addresses the guest: “A throw made in proper sequence counts as an entry; a throw made out of turn earns no tally.”
Second Session

text:

title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
政教焉章亥所步禹跡所及未暇悉論
姑以湖廣言之疆域川澤田賦貢篚見
於禹貢山澤川浸利民畜穀著于職方
可舉其槩歟我
國家受天明命奄甸萬姓際天所覆極地所
載咸入版圖
英宗睿皇帝嘗詔儒臣輯天下圖志以為一統
志頒之學宫傳之天下以著
國家一統之盛信可與夏之禹貢周之職方
===
並垂于不朽豈其他山經地志可比哉
其間所載有所謂名宦有所謂人物以
名宦言之令儀令色頌于周雅三仕三
已見于魯論或功著烏林或威行南服
或興庠序之教或定婚喪之禮或綏懷
遠近得江漢之心或措置屯田圖恢復
之策或有惠愛于復州或著忠節于長
沙其人可得悉數歟以人物言之或有
聲周宣中興之日或立功漢高創業之
punctuated: 政教焉。章亥所步、禹跡所及，未暇悉論。姑以湖廣言之，疆域、川澤、田賦、貢篚見於《禹貢》，山澤、川浸、利民、畜穀著于《職方》，可舉其槩歟？我國家受天明命，奄甸萬姓，際天所覆，極地所載，咸入版圖。英宗睿皇帝嘗詔儒臣輯天下圖志，以為《一統志》，頒之學宫，傳之天下，以著國家一統之盛，信可與夏之《禹貢》、周之《職方》並垂于不朽，豈其他山經地志可比哉？其間所載，有所謂名宦，有所謂人物。以名宦言之，令儀令色頌于《周雅》，三仕三已見于《魯論》；或功著烏林，或威行南服，或興庠序之教，或定婚喪之禮，或綏懷遠近、得江漢之心，或措置屯田、圖恢復之策，或有惠愛于復州，或著忠節于長沙，其人可得悉數歟？以人物言之，或有聲周宣中興之日，或立功漢高創業之
translation_en:
…their government and moral instruction. We have no leisure to discuss exhaustively the places traversed by Zhang Hai [?] or reached by Yu. Let us speak just of Huguang. Its boundaries, rivers and marshes, land taxes, and tribute offerings appear in the Tribute of Yu (Yu gong); its mountains and marshes, rivers and lakes, resources and people, livestock and grain are recorded in the Offices of the Regions (Zhifang). Can you set out their main features?

Our dynasty received Heaven’s illustrious mandate and governs the myriad people. Everything beneath the canopy of heaven and throughout the lands borne by the earth has entered its territorial registers. Emperor Yingzong Rui once commanded Confucian officials to compile illustrated geographical records of the realm into the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Unified Realm (Yitong zhi). It was distributed to the schools and circulated throughout the realm to display the grandeur of our dynasty’s unification. It can surely endure forever alongside the Xia’s Tribute of Yu and the Zhou’s Offices of the Regions. How could other accounts of mountains and geographical records compare with it?

Among its entries are those designated “Distinguished Officials” and those designated “Notable Persons.” As for distinguished officials, one is praised in the Zhou Odes for his fine bearing and gracious countenance; another appears in the Lu Analects as having thrice taken office and thrice been dismissed. Some won distinction for achievements at Wulin; some extended their authority throughout the southern territories; some promoted instruction in local schools; some established rites for marriage and mourning; some pacified and won over those near and far, gaining the allegiance of the people of the Jiang and Han region; some organized military agricultural colonies and planned strategies for recovery of lost territory; some showed benevolence and care at Fuzhou; and some displayed loyalty and integrity at Changsha. Can you enumerate all these men?

As for notable persons, some won renown in the days of revival under King Xuan of Zhou; some rendered meritorious service during Emperor Gao of Han’s founding of his dynasty …

title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
袠或能作訓辭或能通訓典或託志清
雅負社稷之器或清雅知人有水鏡之
稱或首居公位舉奏貪汙或官至宰相
不營產業或以文章魁三試之選或以
道學紹千載之傳其人可得詳陳歟
國家承平百餘年矣自他郡而來蒞茲邦其
勛烈惠政追配昔人者誰歟起南服而
入仕
皇朝其功業節義媲美往哲者誰歟諸士子
===
生長於斯考之熟矣試為我陳之
問孔子之作春秋朱子之作通鑑綱目皆
以史之文寓褒貶之意也先儒謂春秋
大義數十在於大一統正三綱內夏外
夷尊王抑伯而已可得指其實歟或謂
智如子貢未可以言春秋賢如子路未
可以見春秋何以知其然歟至於綱目
之作也褒貶之法殆未易識韓信以反
誅者也特書曰殺謝靈運不忘晉者也
punctuated:
袠，或能作訓辭，或能通訓典，或託志清雅，負社稷之器，或清雅知人，有水鏡之稱，或首居公位，舉奏貪汙，或官至宰相，不營產業，或以文章魁三試之選，或以道學紹千載之傳，其人可得詳陳歟？國家承平百餘年矣，自他郡而來蒞茲邦，其勛烈惠政追配昔人者誰歟？起南服而入仕皇朝，其功業節義媲美往哲者誰歟？諸士子生長於斯，考之熟矣，試為我陳之。

問：孔子之作《春秋》，朱子之作《通鑑綱目》，皆以史之文寓褒貶之意也。先儒謂《春秋》大義數十，在於大一統、正三綱、內夏外夷、尊王抑伯而已，可得指其實歟？或謂智如子貢，未可以言《春秋》；賢如子路，未可以見《春秋》，何以知其然歟？至於《綱目》之作也，褒貶之法殆未易識。韓信以反誅者也，特書曰「殺」；謝靈運不忘晉者也，
translation_en:
…[the opening character 袠 is doubtful here: ?]. Some could compose admonitory pronouncements; some could comprehend the canonical instructions; some set their aspirations on purity and refinement and possessed the capacity to sustain the state; some were pure and refined and discerning judges of men, earning the epithet “water mirror.” Some held the foremost ducal office and impeached the corrupt; some rose to be chief councilors without building up private estates; some, through literary accomplishment, placed first in all three examinations; and some, through the Learning of the Way, carried forward a tradition transmitted over a thousand years. Can you give a detailed account of these men? Our dynasty has enjoyed peace for more than a hundred years. Among those who came from other commanderies to govern this region, whose illustrious achievements and benevolent administration matched those of earlier men? Among those who rose from the southern regions to serve the imperial dynasty, whose achievements, integrity, and righteousness rivaled those of former worthies? You examination candidates were born and raised here and have studied these matters thoroughly. Set them out for me.

Question: When Confucius composed the Spring and Autumn Annals and Master Zhu composed the Outline and Details of the Comprehensive Mirror (Tongjian gangmu), both conveyed praise and blame through historical writing. Earlier Confucian scholars have said that the several dozen great principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals consist simply in honoring unified rule, rectifying the Three Bonds, treating the Xia as insiders and the Yi as outsiders, and exalting true kings while restraining hegemons. Can you identify concrete instances of these principles? Some say that even someone as intelligent as Zigong was not yet qualified to discuss the Spring and Autumn Annals, and even someone as worthy as Zilu was not yet qualified to see it. How do we know this to be so? As for the composition of the Outline and Details, its method of praise and blame is surely not easy to discern. Han Xin was executed for rebellion, yet the text expressly says “killed”; Xie Lingyun was a man who never forgot the Jin dynasty…

title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
特書曰誅管寧卒於魏也而不繫之魏
狄仁傑卒於周也而不繫之周宇文士
及邪諂之臣也而卒書其爵馮道失節
之士也而卒具其官周鼎已遷或謂宜
以東周承其緒何以不之取晋社已屋
或謂宜以宋齊梁陳紹其統何以不之
從袁紹討曹操何以不書其討昭烈誅
楊奉何以不書其誅是盖有深意存焉
願析而言之以見聖賢褒貶之旨
===
問人君南面而聽天下其所倚重而恃力
者相與將耳考之於古陳謨於虞者董
征苗之師迪教於周者著鷹揚之勇固
未有將相之分也三代而下文武始岐
為二以相言之欲斬晁錯與欲斬田仁
者孰賢不知决獄與不問鬭死者孰是
决策以平元濟與决策以誅劉稹者其
功孰大能兼用魏延楊儀與不能兼用
曲端吳玠者其□孰優以將言之二十
punctuated:
特書曰「誅」。管寧卒於魏也，而不繫之魏；狄仁傑卒於周也，而不繫之周。宇文士及邪諂之臣也，而卒書其爵；馮道失節之士也，而卒具其官。周鼎已遷，或謂宜以東周承其緒，何以不之取？晋社已屋，或謂宜以宋齊梁陳紹其統，何以不之從？袁紹討曹操，何以不書其討？昭烈誅楊奉，何以不書其誅？是盖有深意存焉，願析而言之，以見聖賢褒貶之旨。

問：人君南面而聽天下，其所倚重而恃力者，相與將耳。考之於古，陳謨於虞者，董征苗之師；迪教於周者，著鷹揚之勇。固未有將相之分也。三代而下，文武始岐為二。以相言之，欲斬晁錯與欲斬田仁者，孰賢？不知决獄與不問鬭死者，孰是？决策以平元濟與决策以誅劉稹者，其功孰大？能兼用魏延、楊儀與不能兼用曲端、吳玠者，其□孰優？以將言之，二十
translation_en:
…yet it specifically records this as “executed.” Guan Ning died under Wei, yet his death is not assigned to Wei; Di Renjie died under Zhou, yet his death is not assigned to Zhou. Yuwen Shiji was a wicked, sycophantic minister, yet the record of his death includes his noble title; Feng Dao was a man who forfeited his integrity, yet the record of his death gives his official title in full. Once the tripods of Zhou had been transferred, some argued that Eastern Zhou should continue its succession: why was this view not adopted? Once Jin’s altars of state had been roofed over, signifying its extinction, some argued that Song, Qi, Liang, and Chen should carry on its legitimate succession: why was this view not followed? When Yuan Shao campaigned against Cao Cao, why was his action not recorded as a punitive campaign? When Emperor Zhaolie put Yang Feng to death, why was his action not recorded as an execution? There must be profound intentions here. Please analyze and explain them, making clear the purport of the sages’ and worthies’ praise and blame.

Question: When the ruler faces south and governs all under Heaven, those upon whose support and strength he relies are simply his chief ministers and generals. Examining antiquity, we find that the man who presented counsels at the court of Yu also commanded the army campaigning against the Miao; the man who advanced instruction under Zhou also displayed the valor of an eagle soaring aloft. There was originally no distinction between generals and chief ministers. Only after the Three Dynasties did civil and military service diverge into two paths. Speaking of chief ministers: of the man who wished to execute Chao Cuo and the man who wished to execute Tian Ren, which was worthier? Of the man who did not know about adjudicating cases and the man who did not inquire into a death in a fight, which was right? Of the man who resolved upon the strategy that subdued Yuanji and the man who resolved upon the strategy that brought about Liu Zhen’s execution, whose achievement was greater? Comparing the man able to employ both Wei Yan and Yang Yi with the man unable to employ both Qu Duan and Wu Jie, whose [illegible] was superior [?]? Speaking of generals: twenty…

title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
四而封侯與二十八而建節者其成功
孰多以八千兵而敗秦與以五百騎而
敗金者其用兵孰勝斬張用濟於軍門與
不誅蘇建於境外者孰為得擅命以誅
莎車與矯制以誅郅支者孰為非夫隨
陸不武絳灌無文昔人以為耻求其出
將入相文武惟其所用者亦有其人歟
願歷舉而評之以觀予奪之公
問離騷屈原之所作也迹原之仕楚入則
===
圖議政事決定嫌疑出則監察羣下應
對諸侯未為不得志也何為而作是經
歟其經有曰九歌者無非所以寓忠君
愛國之意也而太乙之篇則繼之以湘
君果有議歟曰九章者亦所以寄思君
念國之意也而惜誦之章則繼之以懷
沙果有失歟其美騷者一則謂國風好
色而不淫小雅怨誹而不亂而是經兼
之一則謂至方不能加矩至圓不能加
punctuated:
四而封侯與二十八而建節者，其成功孰多？以八千兵而敗秦與以五百騎而敗金者，其用兵孰勝？斬張用濟於軍門與不誅蘇建於境外者，孰為得？擅命以誅莎車與矯制以誅郅支者，孰為非？夫隨、陸不武，絳、灌無文，昔人以為耻。求其出將入相，文武惟其所用者，亦有其人歟？願歷舉而評之，以觀予奪之公。
問：離騷，屈原之所作也。迹原之仕楚，入則圖議政事，決定嫌疑；出則監察羣下，應對諸侯，未為不得志也。何為而作是經歟？其經有曰九歌者，無非所以寓忠君愛國之意也，而太乙之篇則繼之以湘君，果有議歟？曰九章者，亦所以寄思君念國之意也，而惜誦之章則繼之以懷沙，果有失歟？其美騷者，一則謂「國風好色而不淫，小雅怨誹而不亂」，而是經兼之；一則謂「至方不能加矩，至圓不能加
translation_en:
…twenty-four and was enfeoffed as a marquis, and the one who received a commander's standard at twenty-eight: which achieved more? Between the one who defeated Qin with eight thousand soldiers and the one who defeated Jin with five hundred cavalrymen, which was superior in employing troops? Between the one who executed Zhang Yongji at the army's gate and the one who refrained from executing Su Jian beyond the frontier, which acted rightly? Between the one who assumed authority to execute the ruler of Shache and the one who falsely invoked an imperial decree to execute Zhizhi, which acted wrongly? Sui and Lu lacked martial accomplishments, while Jiang and Guan lacked literary cultivation; men of earlier times regarded this as shameful. Were there men who served as generals in the field and chief ministers at court, applying either civil or military talents as circumstances required? Please enumerate and assess them, so that the impartiality of your praise and blame may be seen.
Question: Encountering Sorrow (Li sao) was composed by Qu Yuan. Considering Yuan's service to Chu, at court he deliberated on affairs of government and resolved doubts; outside it he supervised subordinate officials and dealt with the feudal lords. It cannot be said that he lacked opportunities to realize his ambitions. Why, then, did he compose this classic? In his collection, the pieces called the Nine Songs all convey loyalty to the ruler and love for the state. Yet the poem on Taiyi is followed by the Lord of the Xiang: is there indeed grounds for criticism here? The pieces called the Nine Declarations likewise express longing for the ruler and concern for the state. Yet the declaration Lamenting My Reproaches is followed by Embracing Sand: is there indeed a fault here? Of those who praise Encountering Sorrow, one says, “The Airs of the States express desire without licentiousness; the Lesser Odes express resentment and criticism without disorder,” and that this classic combines both qualities. Another says, “Even perfect squareness cannot surpass the carpenter's square; even perfect roundness cannot surpass …

title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
規而效騷者似之何者為定論歟其議
騷者一則曰鳳凰翔於千仞覽德輝而
下之一則曰臨江瀕而掩涕何有九辨
與九歌何者為過言歟宋玉之招䰟近
乎譎恠而或者謂譏原然歟否歟小山
之招隱晁為高古而或者謂招原然歟
否歟大招何知出於景差之手成相何
知非原之徒抑今之論騷者將以不編
騷於通鑑為失而以所謂風雅再變為
===
===
得歟夫原楚賢諸士子生長於斯必知
之熟講之素請詳以告我
問所貴乎儒者以其博古而通今也不稽
諸古固簡陋不足法不通乎今則迂遠
不可行天下之事多矣姑舉其要者言
之井田不可復矣師丹李安世之制何
者近先王之良法歟封建不可行矣范
氏胡氏之論何者得先王之遺意歟虞
夏殷周之禮不可得而見矣欲復先王
punctuated:
規，而效騷者似之，何者為定論歟？其議騷者，一則曰：「鳳凰翔於千仞，覽德輝而下之。」一則曰：「臨江瀕而掩涕，何有九辨與九歌？」何者為過言歟？宋玉之招䰟近乎譎恠，而或者謂譏原，然歟？否歟？小山之招隱晁為高古，而或者謂招原，然歟？否歟？大招何知出於景差之手？成相何知非原之徒？抑今之論騷者，將以不編騷於通鑑為失，而以所謂風雅再變為得歟？夫原，楚賢，諸士子生長於斯，必知之熟，講之素，請詳以告我。

問：所貴乎儒者，以其博古而通今也。不稽諸古，固簡陋不足法；不通乎今，則迂遠不可行。天下之事多矣，姑舉其要者言之。井田不可復矣，師丹、李安世之制，何者近先王之良法歟？封建不可行矣，范氏、胡氏之論，何者得先王之遺意歟？虞夏殷周之禮不可得而見矣，欲復先王
translation_en:
…the compass, while those who imitate the Li Sao resemble it—which view should be taken as definitive? Among those who criticize the Li Sao, one says, “The phoenix soars a thousand ren high, and descends upon beholding the radiance of virtue.” Another says, “He stood at the river’s edge and wiped away his tears; what use were the Nine Arguments and the Nine Songs?” Which is an excessive statement? Song Yu’s Summoning the Soul borders on the fantastic and strange, yet some say it criticizes Qu Yuan. Is this so or not? Xiaoshan’s Summoning the Recluse is lofty and archaic [?], yet some say it summons Qu Yuan. Is this so or not? How do we know that the Great Summons came from the hand of Jing Cha? How do we know that the author of the Working Songs (Chengxiang) was not a follower of Qu Yuan? Or should those who discuss the Li Sao today regard its omission from the Comprehensive Mirror (Tongjian) as a failing, and the description of it as a further transformation of the Airs and Odes as correct? Qu Yuan was a worthy of Chu. You candidates were born and raised here; surely you know him thoroughly and have long studied him. Please explain these matters to me in detail.

Selecting men through literary compositions was not an ancient practice; if one wishes to make full use of the means of selecting talent, what method is practicable? Appointing men according to formal qualifications and seniority was not an ancient practice; if one wishes to fulfill the proper way of appointing officials, what method is appropriate? These matters are all urgent concerns of the present day. We ask you to weigh ancient institutions, examine what suits present circumstances, and set forth your views, so that we may assess your learning in elucidating fundamental principles and applying them appropriately.

title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
瑟兮僩兮者恂慄也赫兮喧兮者威儀也
何歆
同考試官教諭吳批〔發明君子德容之盛語意精切允宜錄出〕
考試官教諭孫批〔理明詞鬯當是作者〕
考試官教諭李批〔題似易而難發出德容之盛無如此作〕
===
大學釋詩以見君子德容表裏之盛也夫恂慄
者德之存於中威儀者德之著於外也自非明
德君子之止於至善其能然乎傳大學者引淇
澳之詩釋明明德者之止於至善以為君子學
問自脩以盡求之之方則內充外著而有得之
之驗彼詩之所言瑟然而嚴密僩然而武毅者
豈無謂哉蓋言明德君子嚴敬之心恒存乎念
慮警惕之意不忘於須臾戰兢自如凛乎天監
之在兹也戒懼自若悚然上帝之臨女也恂慄
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
「瑟兮僩兮者，恂慄也；赫兮喧兮者，威儀也。」
何歆
同考試官教諭吳批〔發明君子德容之盛，語意精切，允宜錄出。〕
考試官教諭孫批〔理明詞鬯，當是作者。〕
考試官教諭李批〔題似易而難，發出德容之盛，無如此作。〕
大學釋詩，以見君子德容表裏之盛也。夫恂慄者，德之存於中；威儀者，德之著於外也。自非明德君子之止於至善，其能然乎？傳大學者，引淇澳之詩，釋明明德者之止於至善，以為君子學問自脩，以盡求之之方，則內充外著，而有得之之驗。彼詩之所言瑟然而嚴密，僩然而武毅者，豈無謂哉？蓋言明德君子嚴敬之心，恒存乎念慮；警惕之意，不忘於須臾。戰兢自如，凛乎天監之在兹也；戒懼自若，悚然上帝之臨女也。恂慄
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books

“‘Solemn and dignified’ refers to reverent apprehension; ‘illustrious and imposing’ refers to awe-inspiring deportment.”

He Xin

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: “This elucidates the fullness of the gentleman’s virtue and bearing. Its language and meaning are precise and apt; it certainly deserves inclusion.”

Comment by Examiner Sun, Instructor: “The principles are clear and the language flows freely. Surely this is an accomplished writer.”

Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: “The topic seems easy but is difficult. No composition matches this one in bringing out the fullness of virtue and bearing.”

The Great Learning explains the Poetry to reveal the fullness, inward and outward, of the gentleman’s virtue and bearing. Reverent apprehension is virtue abiding within; awe-inspiring deportment is virtue manifesting itself without. Unless a gentleman who makes his virtue bright rests in the highest good, how could he attain this?

The commentator on the Great Learning quotes the poem “The Bend of the Qi” to explain how one who makes bright virtue shine rests in the highest good. His meaning is that, when the gentleman pursues learning and cultivates himself, fully employing the means of seeking it, he becomes fulfilled within and manifests this without, providing evidence that he has attained it. When the poem speaks of solemnity that is exacting and circumspect, and dignity that is valiant and resolute, could these words be without significance?

They mean that the gentleman who makes his virtue bright constantly maintains a sternly reverent heart in his thoughts and reflections, never forgetting vigilance even for an instant. He remains trembling and watchful, awed that Heaven’s scrutiny is here; he remains cautious and fearful, deeply apprehensive that the Lord on High looks down upon you. Reverent apprehension…

title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
如是則怠心不生而無麤疎頽𢙯之失矣德之
存於裏者不其盛乎詩之所謂赫然而宣著喧
然而盛大者亦豈無意哉盖謂明德君子美在
其中而暢於四肢德根於心而形於動靜衣冠
瞻視之尊嚴有威而可畏也動容周旋之中禮
有儀之可象也威儀若是則惰氣不形而無暴
戾傲慢之容矣德之見於表者不亦盛乎君子
德容表裏之盛如此明明德止於至善之驗豈
不於斯而可見哉大抵君子之學以明德為本
===
而明德之要以至善為極明德而不止于至善
是德有未明又何以為新民之地乎大學傳之
三章釋止于至善前既言得之之由此又言得
之之驗末又指其實而歎美之其示人之意深
切矣
師冕見及階子曰階也及席子曰席也皆
坐子告之曰某在斯某在斯師冕出子
張問曰與師言之道與子曰然固相師
之道也
punctuated:
如是，則怠心不生，而無麤疎頽𢙯之失矣。德之存於裏者，不其盛乎？詩之所謂赫然而宣著、喧然而盛大者，亦豈無意哉？盖謂明德君子，美在其中而暢於四肢，德根於心而形於動靜。衣冠瞻視之尊嚴，有威而可畏也；動容周旋之中禮，有儀之可象也。威儀若是，則惰氣不形，而無暴戾傲慢之容矣。德之見於表者，不亦盛乎？君子德容表裏之盛如此，明明德止於至善之驗，豈不於斯而可見哉？大抵君子之學，以明德為本，而明德之要，以至善為極。明德而不止于至善，是德有未明，又何以為新民之地乎？《大學》傳之三章釋止于至善，前既言得之之由，此又言得之之驗，末又指其實而歎美之，其示人之意深切矣。

師冕見，及階，子曰：「階也。」及席，子曰：「席也。」皆坐，子告之曰：「某在斯，某在斯。」師冕出，子張問曰：「與師言之道與？」子曰：「然，固相師之道也。」
translation_en:
…With this disposition, no indolent thought arises, and one avoids the faults of carelessness and laxity [?]. Is not the virtue held within thereby abundant? Nor are the Odes’ descriptions of brilliance that shines forth and splendor that flourishes without meaning. They mean that the gentleman of luminous virtue possesses beauty within, which suffuses his limbs; virtue takes root in his heart and manifests itself in movement and stillness. The dignity of his dress and gaze possesses an awe-inspiring majesty; the conformity of his bearing and movements to ritual provides a deportment worthy of imitation. With such majestic deportment, no indolence shows itself, and there is no appearance of violence or arrogance. Is not the virtue manifested outwardly also abundant? When the gentleman’s virtue and bearing flourish thus, both inwardly and outwardly, can we not see here the evidence that he has manifested luminous virtue and come to rest in the highest good?

In general, the gentleman’s learning takes the manifestation of luminous virtue as its foundation, while the essential task in manifesting luminous virtue is to take the highest good as its ultimate standard. If one manifests luminous virtue but does not come to rest in the highest good, some of that virtue remains unilluminated. How, then, could it provide a foundation for renewing the people? The third chapter of the commentary on the Great Learning explains resting in the highest good. Having first discussed the means of attaining it, it here discusses the evidence of its attainment, and finally points to its actual realization and praises it with admiration. Its intention in instructing people is profound and earnest indeed.

Music Master Mian came to see the Master. When he reached the steps, the Master said, “Here are the steps.” When he reached the mat, the Master said, “Here is the mat.” When everyone was seated, the Master told him, “So-and-so is here, and so-and-so is here.” After Music Master Mian left, Zizhang asked, “Is this the way to speak with a music master?” The Master said, “Yes. This is indeed the way to assist a music master.”

title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
余瑤
同考試官教諭崔批不搜奇獵異而融會傳註成文
時文中之傑然者也是用錄之
同考試官教諭汪批此題人能作之而發明親切者
少是篇詞理俱到必有學之士也
考試官教諭孫批此題不難於體認而難於鋪叙
鋪叙有法者無如此篇宜錄之以範後學
考試官教諭李批詞簡理備當是作者
樂師進見聖人盡夫待之之誠大賢疑問聖人
===
明為相之道盖樂師進見而聖人待之誠者
所以盡相師之道也大賢疑而有問得不明其
為相之道哉昔樂師名冕者進見吾夫子夫
子不惟矜之而且敬之於其及階也則告之以
階使其知所升焉及席也則告之以席使其知
所就焉及衆皆坐之餘又歴告以某在斯某在
斯使其知在坐之人而得以通問焉若是者一
皆聖心天理之流行也及師冕之既出子張竊
窺而有問意謂夫子之於師冕節節而告之諄
punctuated:
余瑤

同考試官教諭汪批：此題人能作之，而發明親切者少。是篇詞理俱到，必有學之士也。

樂師進見，聖人盡夫待之之誠；大賢疑問，聖人明為相之道。盖樂師進見而聖人待之誠者，所以盡相師之道也。大賢疑而有問，得不明其為相之道哉？昔樂師名冕者進見吾夫子，夫子不惟矜之，而且敬之。於其及階也，則告之以階，使其知所升焉；及席也，則告之以席，使其知所就焉。及衆皆坐之餘，又歴告以某在斯、某在斯，使其知在坐之人，而得以通問焉。若是者，一皆聖心天理之流行也。及師冕之既出，子張竊窺而有問，意謂夫子之於師冕，節節而告之，諄

Yu Yao 余瑤

Comment by Associate Examiner Cui, Instructor: He does not seek out the bizarre or hunt for the unusual, but integrates the commentaries and annotations into his composition. This is an outstanding example of contemporary examination prose; for this reason we have selected it for inclusion.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: Anyone can write on this topic, but few elucidate it with precision and direct relevance. This essay is fully accomplished in both expression and reasoning. Its author must be a man of learning.

Comment by Examiner Sun, Instructor: The difficulty of this topic lies not in grasping its meaning but in developing the exposition. No essay matches this one in methodical exposition. It should be included as a model for later students.

Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: Concise in expression and complete in reasoning: this must be the work of an accomplished writer.

When the music master came to pay his respects, the sage received him with the utmost sincerity; when the great worthy raised a question out of uncertainty, the sage explained the proper way to act as a guide. For the sincerity with which the sage received the visiting music master fulfilled the proper way of guiding a music master. When the great worthy expressed his uncertainty in a question, how could the sage fail to explain the proper way to serve as a guide?

Once, a music master named Mian came to pay his respects to our Master. The Master not only felt compassion for him but also treated him with respect. When he reached the steps, the Master told him that these were the steps, so that he would know where to ascend. When he reached the mat, the Master told him that this was the mat, so that he would know where to take his place. After everyone had sat down, the Master further told him in turn, “So-and-so is here; so-and-so is here,” so that he would know who was seated there and could exchange greetings with them. All such actions were manifestations of Heavenly principle flowing through the sage’s heart.

title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
詳而詔之是乃與師言之道歟夫子即告之曰
是與師言之道也彼師冕無目矣階席之處非
所自知我所以告之者相師之道當然也師冕
廢視矣在坐之人非所自識我所以詔之者相
師之道宜爾也吁聖人之待樂師而盡其誠如
此夫豈作意而為之哉抑論之道無往而不在
聖人動靜語默無非道也故其見是人則有待
是人之道遇是事則有處是事之道師冕之見
一事之微耳而聖人待之曲盡其道何莫非道
===
之所在哉學者於此而求之則聖人不侮鰥寡
不虐無告之心亦可見矣
陳良楚產也悅周公仲尼之道北學於中
國北方之學者未能或之先也彼所謂
豪傑之士也
劉渙
同考試官教諭謝批揭書得題本為平易場中作者
不泛則畧此作詞理俱到說出陳良學識之正快愜人心是宜錄出
考試官教諭孫批文以理為主而氣以□之
punctuated:
詳而詔之，是乃與師言之道歟？夫子即告之曰：「是與師言之道也。彼師冕無目矣，階席之處非所自知，我所以告之者，相師之道當然也。師冕廢視矣，在坐之人非所自識，我所以詔之者，相師之道宜爾也。」吁！聖人之待樂師而盡其誠如此，夫豈作意而為之哉？抑論之，道無往而不在，聖人動靜語默無非道也。故其見是人，則有待是人之道；遇是事，則有處是事之道。師冕之見，一事之微耳，而聖人待之曲盡其道，何莫非道之所在哉？學者於此而求之，則聖人不侮鰥寡、不虐無告之心亦可見矣。

陳良，楚產也，悅周公、仲尼之道，北學於中國。北方之學者，未能或之先也。彼所謂豪傑之士也。

劉渙

同考試官教諭謝批：揭書得題，本為平易。場中作者，不泛則畧。此作詞理俱到，說出陳良學識之正，快愜人心，是宜錄出。

考試官教諭孫批：文以理為主，而氣以□之
translation_en:
…explaining to him in detail: was this the proper way to speak to a music master? The Master thereupon told him: “This is the proper way to speak to a music master. That music master Mian is blind: he cannot himself know where the steps and mat are. My telling him is what the way of assisting a music master requires. Music master Mian has lost his sight: he cannot himself recognize those seated there. My informing him is what the way of assisting a music master calls for.” Ah! Such was the complete sincerity with which the sage treated a music master. Could he have acted thus through deliberate contrivance? To discuss this further, the Way is present everywhere. In the sage’s activity and stillness, speech and silence, nothing is other than the Way. Thus, when he meets a particular person, there is a proper way to treat that person; when he encounters a particular matter, there is a proper way to handle that matter. Music master Mian’s visit was merely a minor incident, yet the sage fulfilled the proper way of treating him in every detail. How could any of this fail to embody the Way? If students seek understanding here, they can also perceive the sage’s heart, which neither scorns widowers and widows nor mistreats those with no one to turn to.

“Chen Liang was a native of Chu. Delighting in the Way of the Duke of Zhou and Zhongni, he went north to study in the Central States. Among the scholars of the north, none could surpass him. He was what is called a man of outstanding ability.”

title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
作其庶幾矣
考試官教諭李批詞暢理明足發孟子稱良之意
賢者善變而所得過於人此所以為才德出衆
之士也夫所貴乎豪傑者以其用夏變夷也賢
者生於異邦而慕乎聖道可謂善變者矣豈非
豪傑之士哉昔孟子述陳良之賢以責陳相之
倍師謂夫陳良楚之儒者也生於江漢之間其
去中國也遠矣産於荆衡之域其漸文化也淺
矣然良也不安於陋而慕周公之道北遊中國
===
以學之焉不溺於俗而悅孔子之道北遊諸夏
以學之焉彼禮樂周公之所制作道之所寓也
良則服習乎周公之禮樂詩書孔子之所刪定
道之所存也良則涵泳乎孔子之詩書其慕道
也深其求道也篤雖北方學者素被周公禮樂
之化而其所就未有能出乎其右者也雖中國
學者素聞孔子詩書之教而其所得未有能超
乎其上者也若良者可謂有過人之才而能自
拔於流俗矣可謂有出類之德而能特邁乎等
punctuated:
作，其庶幾矣。
考試官教諭李批：詞暢理明，足發孟子稱良之意。
賢者善變，而所得過於人，此所以為才德出衆之士也。夫所貴乎豪傑者，以其用夏變夷也。賢者生於異邦而慕乎聖道，可謂善變者矣，豈非豪傑之士哉？昔孟子述陳良之賢，以責陳相之倍師，謂夫陳良，楚之儒者也。生於江漢之間，其去中國也遠矣；産於荆衡之域，其漸文化也淺矣。然良也不安於陋，而慕周公之道，北遊中國以學之焉；不溺於俗，而悅孔子之道，北遊諸夏以學之焉。彼禮樂，周公之所制作，道之所寓也，良則服習乎周公之禮樂；詩書，孔子之所刪定，道之所存也，良則涵泳乎孔子之詩書。其慕道也深，其求道也篤。雖北方學者素被周公禮樂之化，而其所就未有能出乎其右者也；雖中國學者素聞孔子詩書之教，而其所得未有能超乎其上者也。若良者，可謂有過人之才，而能自拔於流俗矣；可謂有出類之德，而能特邁乎等
translation_en:
…this composition comes close to that ideal.
Examiner Li, an Instructor, comments: “The language flows freely and the reasoning is clear, fully bringing out Mencius’s intent in praising Liang.”
A worthy person excels at transforming himself, and his attainments surpass those of others: this makes him a man of outstanding talent and virtue. What we prize in an exceptional man is his ability to use the ways of the Xia to transform those of the barbarians. A worthy person who is born in a foreign region yet admires the Way of the sages may indeed be said to excel at transforming himself. Is he not an exceptional man? In former times, Mencius recounted Chen Liang’s worthiness to rebuke Chen Xiang for betraying his teacher. He said that Chen Liang was a Confucian scholar of Chu. Born between the Jiang and Han rivers, he was far from the Central States; a native of the region of Jing and Heng, he had received little exposure to civilizing influences. Yet Liang was not content with uncultivated ways. Admiring the Way of the Duke of Zhou, he traveled north to the Central States to study it. He did not become immersed in vulgar customs. Delighting in the Way of Confucius, he traveled north to the Xia states to study it. Ritual and music were instituted by the Duke of Zhou and embodied the Way; Liang therefore practiced and studied the Duke of Zhou’s ritual and music. The Book of Odes and the Book of Documents were edited and established by Confucius and preserved the Way; Liang therefore immersed himself in Confucius’s Odes and Documents. His admiration for the Way was profound, and his pursuit of it earnest. Although scholars of the north had long been transformed by the Duke of Zhou’s ritual and music, none surpassed him in their achievements. Although scholars of the Central States had long heard the teachings of Confucius’s Odes and Documents, none exceeded him in their attainments. A man such as Liang may be said to possess talent surpassing that of others and to have raised himself above commonplace customs. He may be said to possess virtue beyond the ordinary and to have risen far above his fellow…

title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
倫矣謂之豪傑之士豈不信哉嗟夫陳良生於
楚而學于中國是出幽谷而遷喬木者也陳相
倍其師而學於許行是下喬木而入幽谷者也
是則陳良用夏變夷而陳相變於夷也故孟子
特稱陳良學識之正以責之下文又言聖門弟
子之敬其師雖至死而不忘視彼師死而遂倍
之如相者烏可同年而語哉
易
飛龍在天乃位乎天德
===
何說
同考試官教諭吳批題本正大作者多不會天德
即天位之義往往分而二之間有知者又欲言而未能發揮明
白僅見此篇且辭氣充蔚决非稚筆故録以示
考試官教諭孫批發明天德即天位之義殆無餘蘊
考試官教諭李批文言申九五取象之義此作明甚
文言舉乾九五之象而申以聖德之居乎尊也
盖乾九五以天德而居天位者也爻擬飛龍在
天之象庸非有取諸此歟昔周公繫乾之九五

title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
爻辭曰飛龍在天吾夫子文言復申之謂夫龍
乃陽物而飛則陽性龍至於飛則靈變莫測而
奮起乎天衢之上乾旋坤轉鼓元氣而雷域中
矣豈潜見之可倫乎神化無方而超逸乎雲漢
之表陰吸陽噓騰百川而雨天下矣豈惕躍之
可擬乎此九五之象也而何取於是邪誠以初
二雖陽剛而處地位不可以言位天德惟以九
居五陽剛而遇中正為聖人在天子之位則德
由位顯所以繼天立極而致天下之化成者在
===
是矣是天德也即聖人之天位也而九五有之
非天德之得位者乎三四雖陽剛而當人位亦
不可以言位天德惟五以九居中正而履帝位
為聖人御大寶之尊則位由德稱所以代天理
物而致萬國之咸寧者於是矣是天位也即聖
人之天德也而九五當之非天位之有德者乎
吁此九五所以有飛龍在天之象而為天下之
所利見也歟抑考之文言賛乾之九五則曰位
乎天德釋坤之六五則曰正位居體何歟盖乾
punctuated: 爻辭曰：「飛龍在天。」吾夫子文言復申之，謂夫龍乃陽物，而飛則陽性。龍至於飛，則靈變莫測，而奮起乎天衢之上，乾旋坤轉，鼓元氣而雷域中矣，豈潜見之可倫乎？神化無方，而超逸乎雲漢之表，陰吸陽噓，騰百川而雨天下矣，豈惕躍之可擬乎？此九五之象也，而何取於是邪？誠以初二雖陽剛，而處地位，不可以言位天德。惟以九居五，陽剛而遇中正，為聖人在天子之位，則德由位顯，所以繼天立極而致天下之化成者在是矣。是天德也，即聖人之天位也，而九五有之，非天德之得位者乎？三四雖陽剛，而當人位，亦不可以言位天德。惟五以九居，中正而履帝位，為聖人御大寶之尊，則位由德稱，所以代天理物而致萬國之咸寧者於是矣。是天位也，即聖人之天德也，而九五當之，非天位之有德者乎？吁！此九五所以有飛龍在天之象，而為天下之所利見也歟！抑考之文言，賛乾之九五則曰：「位乎天德。」釋坤之六五則曰：「正位居體。」何歟？盖乾

…the line statement says: “A flying dragon in heaven.” Our Master further elaborated upon this in the Commentary on the Words of the Text (Wenyan), explaining that the dragon is a creature of yang, and flying expresses yang’s nature. When the dragon takes flight, its numinous transformations become unfathomable, and it soars above the thoroughfares of heaven. Heaven revolves and earth turns; it stirs the primal vital force and thunders throughout the world. How could the dragon hidden below or appearing in the field compare with it? Its divine transformations know no bounds, and it rises far beyond the Milky Way. Drawing in yin and breathing out yang, it lifts the waters of the hundred rivers and rains upon all beneath heaven. How could the states of vigilance or leaping compare with it? This is the image of the nine in the fifth place. But why is this image chosen?

It is because, although the first and second lines possess yang firmness, they occupy the positions of earth and cannot be said to “occupy the position of heavenly virtue.” Only when nine occupies the fifth place does yang firmness coincide with centrality and correctness: this represents the sage occupying the position of the Son of Heaven. His virtue is thus made manifest through his position. Herein lies the means by which he carries on Heaven’s work, establishes the supreme standard, and brings the transformation of all beneath heaven to completion. This heavenly virtue is precisely the sage’s heavenly position, and the nine in the fifth place possesses it. Is this not heavenly virtue attaining its proper position?

Although the third and fourth lines possess yang firmness, they occupy the positions of humanity and likewise cannot be said to “occupy the position of heavenly virtue.” Only when the fifth place is occupied by nine does one, central and correct, ascend the imperial position: this represents the sage holding the exalted dignity of the throne. His position thus finds its fitting counterpart in his virtue. Herein lies the means by which he orders all things on Heaven’s behalf and brings peace to the myriad states. This heavenly position is precisely the sage’s heavenly virtue, and the nine in the fifth place occupies it. Is this not the heavenly position being endowed with virtue?

Ah! Is this why the nine in the fifth place has the image of “a flying dragon in heaven,” and why all beneath heaven benefit from seeing him? Yet, examining the Commentary on the Words of the Text, we find that in praising the nine in the fifth place of Qian it says, “He occupies the position of heavenly virtue,” whereas in explaining the six in the fifth place of Kun it says, “He occupies the correct position and abides in the substance.” Why is this? title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
非術數之知得其正而非苛察之明矣然周萬
物者知之體也其見於事也酬酢應變之曲當
因時舉措之咸宜其用有以行權焉濟天下者
仁之用也其本諸己也貞靜而不入於變詐純
一而不流於邪僻其體有以守正焉有周物之
體而達諸行權之用知已深矣至於靜與天俱
而默契乎天命流行賦予之妙動與天游而貫
徹乎事物所以當然之故則心廣體胖而自无
所憂其知之益深也為何如有濟物之用而本
===
諸守正之體仁已篤矣至於无入不得而渾乎
天地生物之心隨寓皆安而篤乎本心全體之
德則民胞物與而自无不愛其仁之益篤也又
何如乎聖人用易而盡知仁之性如此此其所
以與天地相似而不違也歟雖然人得天地之
理以為性本與天地同體也但人汩於形氣而
自失之耳聖人性之者也窮理盡性雖不假乎
易而亦未嘗不用乎易所以先天而天弗違後
天而奉天時直與天地同流而不悖同體而无
punctuated:
非術數之知，得其正而非苛察之明矣。然周萬物者，知之體也；其見於事也，酬酢應變之曲當，因時舉措之咸宜，其用有以行權焉。濟天下者，仁之用也；其本諸己也，貞靜而不入於變詐，純一而不流於邪僻，其體有以守正焉。有周物之體而達諸行權之用，知已深矣。至於靜與天俱而默契乎天命流行賦予之妙，動與天游而貫徹乎事物所以當然之故，則心廣體胖而自无所憂，其知之益深也為何如？有濟物之用而本諸守正之體，仁已篤矣。至於无入不得而渾乎天地生物之心，隨寓皆安而篤乎本心全體之德，則民胞物與而自无不愛，其仁之益篤也又何如乎？聖人用易而盡知仁之性如此，此其所以與天地相似而不違也歟？
雖然，人得天地之理以為性，本與天地同體也，但人汩於形氣而自失之耳。聖人性之者也，窮理盡性，雖不假乎易，而亦未嘗不用乎易，所以先天而天弗違，後天而奉天時，直與天地同流而不悖，同體而无
translation_en:
…and is not the cleverness of techniques and calculations; it attains correctness and is not the discernment of excessively exacting scrutiny. Now, encompassing the myriad things is the substance of wisdom. When manifested in affairs, its responses to others and adaptations to change are fitting in every particular, and its actions suit every occasion: in its operation, it can thus exercise discretion. Bringing benefit to all under Heaven is the operation of benevolence. As rooted in oneself, it is steadfast and still, never descending into deceit; pure and undivided, never drifting into perversity. In its substance, it can thus preserve rectitude.
With the substance that encompasses things extending into the operation that exercises discretion, wisdom is already profound. Yet when, in stillness, one abides with Heaven and tacitly accords with the marvel of Heaven’s mandate flowing forth and bestowing endowments, and, in activity, one moves with Heaven and fully comprehends the reasons why affairs and things ought to be as they are, the mind becomes expansive and the body at ease, and one is naturally free from anxiety. How much more profound, then, is such wisdom! With the operation that benefits things rooted in the substance that preserves rectitude, benevolence is already steadfast. Yet when one finds fulfillment in every situation and becomes wholly one with the mind of Heaven and Earth that gives life to things, rests at ease wherever one finds oneself, and firmly embodies the virtue of the original mind in its entirety, one regards the people as siblings and all things as companions, and naturally loves all without exception. How much more steadfast, then, is such benevolence! In this way the sage uses the Changes to fulfill the nature of wisdom and benevolence. Is this not why the sage resembles Heaven and Earth and does not diverge from them?

Thus, when he precedes Heaven, Heaven does not oppose him; when he follows Heaven, he accords with Heaven’s seasons. translation_en:
…With one sweep of the imperial spear, the Jurchen army collapses by night; when the yellow battle-axe is wielded, the forces of the rebel Yu flee in secret. Intent on recovering the ancestral inheritance—the old blue felt—you consult the gray-haired elders. Thus even one so impractical and inept as I has received your discerning acceptance. How could your servant fail to exert his meager abilities to the utmost, in grateful response to your attentive favor?

May we perform the feng sacrifice on Mount Langxu and the shan sacrifice on Mount Guyan, thereby bringing peace to the spirits of the nine ancestral temples; may we drive the enemy from their frontier outposts and compel Xiutu to submit, hoping to efface the humiliation of a hundred kings. We shall presently see the entire territory of Yan restored to the domain of the Great Song. As civil virtue spreads far and wide, may we witness the transforming power of the shield dance; as royal policies are fully realized, may we sing again the ode “Ever Martial.”

Your servant, looking up to Heaven and reverently toward Your Majesty, cannot contain his intense emotion and profound trepidation. I respectfully submit this memorial to convey my thanks for your imperial hearing.

title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
有圖以著山林川澤之險阨如所謂輿地
圖是已必有志以紀貢賦人物之繁盛如
所謂寰宇志是已明君賢相知其阨塞而
爲吾兵險易之備察其風俗而爲吾政弛
張之宜夫豈苟然哉姑以湖廣言之荆及
衡陽其疆域也江漢雲夢其川澤也其田
則下中其賦則上下貢則羽毛齒革之屬
篚則玄纁璣組之類禹貢所載然也鎮曰
衡山藪曰雲夢其川江漢其浸潁湛其利
===
丹銀齒革其民一男二女其畜鳥獸其穀
宜稻職方氏所紀然也是則湖廣山川名
物載于夏書紀于周禮垂之萬世而爲經
矣洪惟
聖朝受天明命奄有萬邦章亥所步悉歸版圖
之内禹跡所及咸在統御之中
英宗睿皇帝爰命儒臣發祕閣所藏採郡國所
上編輯
大明一統志頒之學官傳之天下以昭
punctuated:
有圖以著山林川澤之險阨，如所謂輿地圖是已；必有志以紀貢賦人物之繁盛，如所謂寰宇志是已。明君賢相知其阨塞，而爲吾兵險易之備；察其風俗，而爲吾政弛張之宜。夫豈苟然哉？姑以湖廣言之：荆及衡陽，其疆域也；江漢雲夢，其川澤也。其田則下中，其賦則上下，貢則羽毛齒革之屬，篚則玄纁璣組之類，《禹貢》所載然也。鎮曰衡山，藪曰雲夢，其川江漢，其浸潁湛，其利丹銀齒革，其民一男二女，其畜鳥獸，其穀宜稻，《職方氏》所紀然也。是則湖廣山川名物，載于《夏書》，紀于《周禮》，垂之萬世而爲經矣。
洪惟聖朝受天明命，奄有萬邦，章亥所步，悉歸版圖之内；禹跡所及，咸在統御之中。英宗睿皇帝爰命儒臣發祕閣所藏，採郡國所上，編輯《大明一統志》，頒之學官，傳之天下，以昭
translation_en:
…there were maps to show the difficult terrain and narrow passes of mountains, forests, rivers, and marshes, such as what are called geographical maps; there were necessarily also gazetteers to record the abundance of tribute and taxes, people and products, such as the Gazetteer of the Realm. Enlightened rulers and worthy chief councillors understood these strategic barriers and prepared their armies for difficult and easy terrain alike; they examined local customs and adjusted the severity or leniency of their administration accordingly. How could this have been done casually?
Take Huguang, for example: Jing and the southern slopes of Mount Heng define its territory; the Jiang and Han rivers and Yunmeng constitute its rivers and marshes. Its fields were rated lower-middle, and its tax assessment upper-lower. Its tribute included feathers, hair, ivory, and hides; its basket offerings included dark and crimson silks and pearl-strung cords. Such is the account in the Tribute of Yu. Its principal mountain was called Hengshan, and its great marsh Yunmeng; its rivers were the Jiang and Han, and its reservoirs the Ying and Zhan [?]. Its valuable products were cinnabar, silver, ivory, and hides; its population comprised one man for every two women; its domestic animals were birds and beasts; and rice was its suitable grain. Such is the record in the Officers of the Regions. Thus Huguang’s mountains and rivers, notable features and products were recorded in the Documents of Xia and the Rites of Zhou, handed down for ten thousand generations as canonical writings.
We reverently reflect that our sagely dynasty received Heaven’s illustrious mandate and came to possess all the myriad states. All the lands traversed by Zhang and Hai [?] fall within its registered territory, and all the places reached by Yu lie under its rule. Emperor Yingzong Rui thereupon commanded his Confucian officials to open the holdings of the imperial library and gather the materials submitted by the prefectures and territories, compiling the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Great Ming. He distributed it to the education officials and circulated it throughout the realm, in order to display…

title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
國家一統之盛誠可與夏之禹貢周之職方
並垂于不朽也其間所載有所謂名宦有
所謂人物以名宦言之仲山甫令儀令色
為周名臣子文三仕三已為楚賢相周瑜
當炎光將燼之際功著于烏林劉弘當金
行失馭之時威行於南服衛颯脩庠序之
教而文治興欒巴定婚喪之禮而舊俗變
綏懷遠近得江漢之心則有如羊祜措置
屯田圖恢復之舉則有如岳飛狄仁傑出
===
刺復州其惠愛可稱也李芾死節長沙其
忠義可仰也此皆吾荆南之名宦也以人
物言之吉甫之勲烈有聲宣王中興之日
梅鋗之材武立功漢高創業之初制誥典
贍無愧能作訓辭之觀射父則歐陽玄其
人博通經史無愧能通訓典之倚相則黃
香其人託志忠雅負社稷之器非蔣琬乎
清雅知人有水鑑之稱非司馬徽乎黃瓊
首居公位舉奏貪汙其忠鯁可知岑文本
punctuated:
國家一統之盛，誠可與夏之《禹貢》、周之《職方》並垂于不朽也。其間所載，有所謂名宦，有所謂人物。以名宦言之，仲山甫令儀令色，為周名臣；子文三仕三已，為楚賢相；周瑜當炎光將燼之際，功著于烏林；劉弘當金行失馭之時，威行於南服；衛颯脩庠序之教，而文治興；欒巴定婚喪之禮，而舊俗變。綏懷遠近，得江漢之心，則有如羊祜；措置屯田，圖恢復之舉，則有如岳飛。狄仁傑出刺復州，其惠愛可稱也；李芾死節長沙，其忠義可仰也。此皆吾荆南之名宦也。
以人物言之，吉甫之勲烈，有聲宣王中興之日；梅鋗之材武，立功漢高創業之初。制誥典贍，無愧能作訓辭之觀射父，則歐陽玄其人；博通經史，無愧能通訓典之倚相，則黃香其人。託志忠雅，負社稷之器，非蔣琬乎？清雅知人，有水鑑之稱，非司馬徽乎？黃瓊首居公位，舉奏貪汙，其忠鯁可知。岑文本
translation_en:
…the splendor of the realm’s unification, which may indeed endure imperishably alongside the Xia’s Tribute of Yu and the Zhou’s Offices of the Regions. Among its contents are those designated “Eminent Officials” and those designated “Notable Persons.” To speak of eminent officials: Zhong Shanfu, with his admirable deportment and bearing, was a renowned minister of Zhou; Ziwen, who took office three times and was dismissed three times, was a worthy chief minister of Chu. Zhou Yu distinguished himself at Wulin when the fiery radiance of the Han was about to gutter out; Liu Hong made his authority felt throughout the southern territories when the Jin dynasty, associated with the Metal phase, lost control of government. Wei Sa cultivated instruction in the local schools, and civil governance flourished; Luan Ba established rites for marriage and mourning, and old customs changed. Among those who brought peace and won allegiance far and near, gaining the hearts of the people of the Jiang and Han regions, was Yang Hu; among those who organized agricultural colonies and planned the recovery of lost territory was Yue Fei. Di Renjie went out to serve as Prefect of Fuzhou, and his benevolent care deserves praise; Li Fu died upholding his integrity at Changsha, and his loyalty and righteousness deserve admiration. These were all eminent officials of our Jingnan.
To speak of notable persons: Jifu’s glorious achievements won renown during King Xuan’s restoration of Zhou; Mei Xuan’s military talent earned him distinction at the beginning of Han Gaozu’s founding enterprise. For dignified and richly composed imperial proclamations, the man worthy of comparison with Guan Shefu, who could compose admonitory pronouncements, was Ouyang Xuan. For broad mastery of the classics and histories, the man worthy of comparison with Yixiang, who comprehended the ancient instructions and canons, was Huang Xiang. Was it not Jiang Wan who devoted his aspirations to loyalty and rectitude and possessed the capacity to sustain the state? Was it not Sima Hui who, refined and discerning of men, was praised as a mirror of clear water? Upon first attaining a position among the Three Dukes, Huang Qiong impeached corrupt officials: his loyalty and forthrightness are evident. Cen Wenben…

title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
官至宰相不營產業其節儉可見馮京以
文章魁三試之選周茂叔以道學紹千載
之傳此皆吾荆南之人物也我
國家承平百有餘年矣或自他郡而來蒞兹
邦若鄧愈之鎮襄陽恩敷襄漢四境以寧
陶安之守黃州安輯民庶政務一新其勲
烈惠政足以追配昔人而無愧或起南服
而入仕
皇朝若楊文定公謙厚温恭典機務於
===
内閣何忠節公讜言正色著忠義于南交其
功業節義足以媲美往哲而有光嗟夫萬
古此山川則萬古此人物孰謂今人之不
如古又焉知後来之不如今哉愚也生長
是邦撫汗簡之沉馨仰前脩之芳躅毎感
慨思自勵焉倘執事進而敎之敢不近法
文定遠追吉甫以效其尺寸而垂名竹帛
乎
第貳問
punctuated:
官至宰相，不營產業，其節儉可見。馮京以文章魁三試之選，周茂叔以道學紹千載之傳，此皆吾荆南之人物也。我國家承平百有餘年矣。或自他郡而來蒞兹邦，若鄧愈之鎮襄陽，恩敷襄漢，四境以寧；陶安之守黃州，安輯民庶，政務一新。其勲烈惠政，足以追配昔人而無愧。或起南服而入仕皇朝，若楊文定公謙厚温恭，典機務於内閣；何忠節公讜言正色，著忠義于南交。其功業節義，足以媲美往哲而有光。嗟夫！萬古此山川，則萬古此人物。孰謂今人之不如古，又焉知後来之不如今哉？愚也生長是邦，撫汗簡之沉馨，仰前脩之芳躅，毎感慨思自勵焉。倘執事進而敎之，敢不近法文定，遠追吉甫，以效其尺寸，而垂名竹帛乎？

第貳問
translation_en:
… rose to the office of chief councilor but did not amass property: his frugality is plain to see. Feng Jing’s literary compositions won him first place in all three examinations; Zhou Maoshu, through his learning of the Way, carried forward a tradition reaching back a thousand years. These are all eminent men of our Jingnan. Our dynasty has enjoyed peace for more than a hundred years. Some came from other prefectures to govern this region. Deng Yu, for example, commanded at Xiangyang: his beneficence spread throughout the Xiangyang and Han River region, bringing peace within its borders. Tao An, as prefect of Huangzhou, settled and comforted the common people and thoroughly renewed its administration. Their illustrious achievements and benevolent government can stand beside those of their predecessors without shame. Others arose in the southern region and entered the service of the imperial dynasty. Lord Yang, posthumously titled Wending, was modest, generous, gentle, and respectful, and directed crucial affairs in the Grand Secretariat. Lord He, posthumously titled Zhongjie, spoke forthrightly with a grave countenance and made his loyalty and righteousness manifest in Nanjiao. Their accomplishments and moral integrity can rival those of earlier worthies and shine with equal brilliance. Ah! These mountains and rivers endure through the ages, and so too do the eminent men they produce. Who says that people today cannot equal those of antiquity? And how can we know that those yet to come will not equal those of today? I, unworthy though I am, was born and raised in this region. As I ponder the lingering fragrance of the historical records and look up to the noble footsteps of former worthies, I am often deeply moved and resolve to spur myself onward. If you, honored sir, would advance and instruct me, how could I dare fail to model myself on Wending in the recent past and emulate Jifu in the distant past, contributing my own small measure of service and leaving my name in the historical records?

title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
何說
同考試官教諭吳批本房幾三百卷連日披閱初二
場儘有可意者至三場多掛一漏百令人厭觀此卷五策俱稱春秋
綱目一策尤深得聖賢褒貶之㫖况前二場已在優等取冠多士允愜
輿論
考試官教諭孫批末場士子多為此策所困往往
敷衍問目而已此卷於二書事實一一剖析詳明不啻繩貫櫛比
然必老學也允宜高薦
考試官教諭李批春秋之㫖知之者多綱目書法
===
鮮有知者此卷條答無遺而文足以發之必有學有識士也彼敷
衍問目者風斯下矣
春秋作於聖人有以昭百王之典禮綱目
作於大儒有以定千載之是非此春秋所
以為經世之大法綱目所以為致治之明
鑑也非道足以周天下之用智足以通難
知之意文足以發難顯之情者其孰能作
之哉慨自周東遷而典禮紊矣於是孔子
出而春秋作焉宋南渡而是非昧矣於是
punctuated:
何說。

同考試官教諭吳批：本房幾三百卷，連日披閱，初二場儘有可意者，至三場，多掛一漏百，令人厭觀。此卷五策俱稱，《春秋》《綱目》一策尤深得聖賢褒貶之㫖。况前二場已在優等，取冠多士，允愜輿論。

考試官教諭孫批：末場士子多為此策所困，往往敷衍問目而已。此卷於二書事實，一一剖析詳明，不啻繩貫櫛比，然必老學也，允宜高薦。

考試官教諭李批：《春秋》之㫖，知之者多；《綱目》書法，鮮有知者。此卷條答無遺，而文足以發之，必有學有識士也。彼敷衍問目者，風斯下矣。

《春秋》作於聖人，有以昭百王之典禮；《綱目》作於大儒，有以定千載之是非。此《春秋》所以為經世之大法，《綱目》所以為致治之明鑑也。非道足以周天下之用、智足以通難知之意、文足以發難顯之情者，其孰能作之哉？慨自周東遷而典禮紊矣，於是孔子出而《春秋》作焉；宋南渡而是非昧矣，於是
translation_en:
He Shuo 何說.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: In this examining room there were nearly three hundred scripts, which I read over successive days. In the first two sessions there were quite a few satisfactory answers, but in the third, many touched on one point while omitting a hundred, making them tiresome to read. All five policy essays in this script are commendable. The essay on the Spring and Autumn Annals and the Outline and Details of the Comprehensive Mirror (Gangmu) particularly grasps the profound intent of the sages and worthies in assigning praise and blame. Moreover, his first two sessions were already graded superior. Ranking him first among the candidates truly accords with the general judgment.

Comment by Examiner Sun, Instructor: In the final session, many candidates were stymied by this policy question and often merely elaborated on the wording of the question. This script analyzes the historical particulars in the two books one by one, clearly and thoroughly, arranging them like objects strung on a cord or the teeth of a comb. Surely its author is a seasoned scholar; he truly deserves recommendation at a high rank.

Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: Many understand the intent of the Spring and Autumn Annals, but few understand the conventions of historical writing in the Outline and Details. This script answers every point without omission, and its prose fully elucidates them. Its author must be a man of learning and discernment. Those who merely elaborate on the wording of the question bow before him like grass before the wind.

The Spring and Autumn Annals was composed by a sage, thereby illuminating the institutions and rites of the hundred kings; the Outline and Details was composed by a great Confucian scholar, thereby settling questions of right and wrong over a thousand years. This is why the Spring and Autumn Annals serves as the great standard for ordering the world, and the Outline and Details as a clear mirror for achieving good government. Who could compose such works unless his command of the Way sufficed to meet all the needs of the world, his wisdom to penetrate meanings difficult to comprehend, and his literary skill to express circumstances difficult to reveal? Alas, after the Zhou moved east, institutions and rites fell into disorder. Thereupon Confucius appeared, and the Spring and Autumn Annals was composed. After the Song moved south, right and wrong became obscured. Thereupon…

text:
朱子出而綱目作焉以春秋言之書王而
次於正書王而次於春揭一王之號於一
歲之首所以大一統也河陽書狩而君臣
之綱正子同書生而與子之法明如齊同
行見夫之不夫會禖獨往見婦之不婦所
以正三綱也楚稱王矣則書楚子越嘗霸
矣則稱於越其内夏外夷之法嚴矣葵丘
緣陵之城予其事而責其專城濮踐土之
舉大其功而著其譎其尊王抑霸之旨著
===
矣書閏月不告朔猶朝于廟春秋愛禮之
意也而子貢欲去告朔之餼羊是子貢之
智未可以言春秋也書趙鞅帥師納衞世
子蒯聵于戚此春秋正名之意也而子路
乃以正名為迂是子路之賢未可以見春
秋也以綱目言之韓信未有反心也舍人
上變之辭欲加之罪耳故書以殺謝靈運
已臣於宋也韓亡秦帝之詩借以自文耳
故正其誅管寧雖卒于魏而不受魏之官
punctuated:
朱子出而綱目作焉。以春秋言之，書王而次於正，書王而次於春，揭一王之號於一歲之首，所以大一統也。河陽書狩，而君臣之綱正；子同書生，而與子之法明。如齊同行，見夫之不夫；會禖獨往，見婦之不婦，所以正三綱也。楚稱王矣，則書楚子；越嘗霸矣，則稱於越，其内夏外夷之法嚴矣。葵丘、緣陵之城，予其事而責其專；城濮、踐土之舉，大其功而著其譎，其尊王抑霸之旨著矣。書「閏月不告朔，猶朝于廟」，春秋愛禮之意也，而子貢欲去告朔之餼羊，是子貢之智未可以言春秋也。書「趙鞅帥師納衞世子蒯聵于戚」，此春秋正名之意也，而子路乃以正名為迂，是子路之賢未可以見春秋也。

以綱目言之，韓信未有反心也，舍人上變之辭，欲加之罪耳，故書以殺；謝靈運已臣於宋也，韓亡秦帝之詩，借以自文耳，故正其誅。管寧雖卒于魏，而不受魏之官
translation_en:
…Master Zhu emerged, and the Outline and Details of the Comprehensive Mirror (Gangmu) was composed. To speak first of the Spring and Autumn Annals: it writes “king” after “first month,” and “king” after “spring” [?]. By placing the designation of the one king at the beginning of the year, it exalts unity under a single sovereign. By recording the event at Heyang as a royal hunt, it rectifies the cardinal relationship between ruler and minister; by recording the birth of the son Tong, it clarifies the rule for recognizing a son as heir. Traveling together to Qi reveals a husband's failure to act as a husband; going alone to the meeting at Mei [?] reveals a wife's failure to act as a wife. In this way it rectifies the Three Cardinal Relationships. Though the ruler of Chu styled himself king, it writes “Viscount of Chu”; though Yue had exercised hegemony, it calls it “Yuyue.” Strict indeed is its rule of treating the Chinese states as insiders and the non-Chinese as outsiders. In the fortification of Kuiqiu [?] and Yuanling, it approves the undertaking but censures the unauthorized exercise of power; in the actions at Chengpu and Jiantu, it magnifies the achievement but exposes the deceit. Its purpose of honoring the king and restraining the hegemons is thus manifest. It records: “In the intercalary month, the announcement of the new moon was omitted, yet the court observance at the ancestral temple was still performed.” This expresses the Annals' concern to preserve ritual. Yet Zigong wished to dispense with the sacrificial sheep supplied for announcing the new moon. Thus even Zigong's wisdom was insufficient for discussing the Annals. It records: “Zhao Yang led an army to install Kuai Kui, heir apparent of Wei, at Qi.” This expresses the Annals' purpose of rectifying names. Yet Zilu regarded the rectification of names as impractical. Thus even Zilu's worthiness was insufficient for understanding the Annals.

To speak of the Outline and Details: Han Xin had harbored no intention of rebellion. His retainer's denunciation was merely an attempt to fasten a charge upon him; hence the work records his death as a killing. Xie Lingyun had already become a subject of the Song. His verse about Han's fall and Qin's assumption of imperial rule merely served to cloak his own conduct; hence the work affirms the justice of his execution. Although Guan Ning died in Wei, he did not accept office from Wei…

title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
爵故不係之魏者所以著其潔身之節狄
仁傑雖仕于周而不忘唐之宗社故不係
之周者所以表其忠君之誠宇文士及邪
諂之臣也而卒書其爵非責太宗親狎佞
人歟馮道失節之士也而卒書其官非責
時君寵遇失節歟周鼎已遷葉氏謂宜繼
東周承其緒而綱目不之取者東周亦諸
侯耳非有恢復舊物之志也晉社已屋胡
明仲謂宜以宋齊梁陳紹其統而綱目不
===
之從者宋齊梁陳皆偏據耳非有統一天
下之志也袁紹討曹操嘗聲操之罪矣不
書其討者志在兼併初非為漢計也昭烈
誅楊奉彼固有罪可誅矣不書其誅者誘
而殺之不得為天討也噫春秋作於前而
典禮以明綱目作於後而是非以定聖賢
有功於天下有功於萬世為何如哉管見
區區未知是否惟執事進而教之幸甚
第叁問
punctuated:
爵，故不係之魏者，所以著其潔身之節。狄仁傑雖仕于周，而不忘唐之宗社，故不係之周者，所以表其忠君之誠。宇文士及，邪諂之臣也，而卒書其爵，非責太宗親狎佞人歟？馮道，失節之士也，而卒書其官，非責時君寵遇失節歟？周鼎已遷，葉氏謂宜繼東周承其緒，而綱目不之取者，東周亦諸侯耳，非有恢復舊物之志也。晉社已屋，胡明仲謂宜以宋齊梁陳紹其統，而綱目不之從者，宋齊梁陳皆偏據耳，非有統一天下之志也。袁紹討曹操，嘗聲操之罪矣，不書其討者，志在兼併，初非為漢計也。昭烈誅楊奉，彼固有罪可誅矣，不書其誅者，誘而殺之，不得為天討也。噫！春秋作於前，而典禮以明；綱目作於後，而是非以定。聖賢有功於天下，有功於萬世，為何如哉！管見區區，未知是否，惟執事進而教之，幸甚。
第叁問
translation_en:
…rank; thus, by not identifying him with Wei, it makes manifest his integrity in keeping himself unsullied. Although Di Renjie served Zhou, he never forgot the ancestral temples and altars of Tang. Thus, by not identifying him with Zhou, it displays the sincerity of his loyalty to his sovereign. Yuwen Shiji was a wicked, flattering minister, yet the entry recording his death gives his noble rank. Does this not rebuke Taizong for his intimacy with a sycophant? Feng Dao was a man who forfeited his integrity, yet the entry recording his death gives his official title. Does this not rebuke the rulers of his time for favoring and honoring a man without integrity?
The tripods of Zhou had already been removed. Master Ye held that Eastern Zhou should have been treated as continuing its succession, but the Outline and Details (Gangmu) did not adopt this view: Eastern Zhou was merely another feudal state and had no ambition to restore the former patrimony. The altars of Jin had already been roofed over, marking the dynasty’s fall. Hu Mingzhong held that Song, Qi, Liang, and Chen should have been treated as continuing its legitimate succession, but the Outline and Details did not follow this view: Song, Qi, Liang, and Chen each controlled only part of the realm and had no ambition to unify all under Heaven.
When Yuan Shao campaigned against Cao Cao, he publicly proclaimed Cao’s crimes. Yet the work does not record his action as a punitive expedition, because his purpose was annexation; from the outset, he was not acting for the sake of Han. When Zhaolie killed Yang Feng, Yang certainly had committed crimes punishable by death. Yet the work does not record the killing as a rightful execution, because he lured Yang into a trap and killed him: this could not count as Heaven’s punishment.
Ah! The Spring and Autumn Annals was composed earlier, and thereby the canonical institutions and rites were clarified; the Outline and Details was composed later, and thereby right and wrong were determined. How great are the services of the sages and worthies to all under Heaven and to all generations! These are merely my narrow views, and I do not know whether they are correct. I would be most fortunate if you would advance me through your instruction.
Third Question

title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
宋奎
同考試官訓導張批歷舉三代而下將相事蹟而於
非之末獨推許范虞數君子非灼有定見者不能異時登庸必能樹
勳業而著聲光也健羡健羡
考試官教諭孫批將相一策能條答者固多然議
奪品題之當似此者絕少且文氣春容辭整有如天馬行空步驟不
凡吾於此子讓之一頭地矣
考試官教諭李批將相之策多為所窘此作事實
無遺必熟於評品人物者也
===
秉鈞當軸以熙帝載固莫重於相擁旄仗
鉞以揚天威尤莫急於將相得其人則德
教敷而四海以均將得其人則威武振而
四夷以靖有天下者其可不擇文武偉人
以當將相重任邪執事以古之將相下詢
承學敢不攄所聞以復明問之萬一乎夫
人君南面而聽天下其所倚重而恃力者
相與將耳考之於古大禹告其君以克艱
之謨矣而征苗之師禹實統之太公迪其
punctuated:
宋奎

同考試官訓導張批：歷舉三代而下將相事蹟，而於非之末，獨推許范虞數君子，非灼有定見者不能。異時登庸，必能樹勳業而著聲光也。健羡，健羡！

考試官教諭孫批：將相一策，能條答者固多，然議奪品題之當似此者絕少。且文氣春容，辭整，有如天馬行空，步驟不凡。吾於此子讓之一頭地矣。

考試官教諭李批：將相之策，多為所窘。此作事實無遺，必熟於評品人物者也。

秉鈞當軸以熙帝載，固莫重於相；擁旄仗鉞以揚天威，尤莫急於將。相得其人，則德教敷而四海以均；將得其人，則威武振而四夷以靖。有天下者，其可不擇文武偉人以當將相重任邪？執事以古之將相下詢承學，敢不攄所聞以復明問之萬一乎？夫人君南面而聽天下，其所倚重而恃力者，相與將耳。考之於古，大禹告其君以克艱之謨矣，而征苗之師，禹實統之。太公迪其

title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
君以兵書之戒矣而牧野之兵太公實将
之當是時人皆全才出焉而將則折衝萬
里之外入焉而相則論道一堂之上固未
有將相之分也三代而下文武始岐而為
二以相言之申屠嘉欲斬鼂錯與劉屈氂
欲斬田仁其欲舉相職雖同然嘉之忠言
謇謇賢於屈氂之終陷刑戮也陳平不知
决獄與丙吉不問鬭死其能知相體雖一
然平之元勛赫赫優於吉之無所建明也
===
裴度决策以平淮蔡李德裕决策以平澤
潞功皆大矣然度不立朋黨而德裕立黨
相攻是度之德量優於德裕也孔明相昭
烈於炎燼重噓之時張浚相高宗於宋室
再造之際忠皆著矣然孔明能兼用魏延
楊儀而浚不能兼用曲端吳玠是浚之材
器劣於孔明也以將言之鄧禹二十四而
封侯荀羨二十八而建節皆以年少而立
功也然禹為東都元勛而羨之功業未著
punctuated: 君以兵書之戒矣，而牧野之兵，太公實将之。當是時，人皆全才，出焉而將，則折衝萬里之外；入焉而相，則論道一堂之上，固未有將相之分也。三代而下，文武始岐而為二。以相言之，申屠嘉欲斬鼂錯，與劉屈氂欲斬田仁，其欲舉相職雖同，然嘉之忠言謇謇，賢於屈氂之終陷刑戮也。陳平不知决獄，與丙吉不問鬭死，其能知相體雖一，然平之元勛赫赫，優於吉之無所建明也。裴度决策以平淮蔡，李德裕决策以平澤潞，功皆大矣，然度不立朋黨，而德裕立黨相攻，是度之德量優於德裕也。孔明相昭烈於炎燼重噓之時，張浚相高宗於宋室再造之際，忠皆著矣，然孔明能兼用魏延、楊儀，而浚不能兼用曲端、吳玠，是浚之材器劣於孔明也。以將言之，鄧禹二十四而封侯，荀羨二十八而建節，皆以年少而立功也，然禹為東都元勛，而羨之功業未著
translation_en:
…his ruler with the admonitions of the military writings, and it was indeed Taigong who commanded the troops at Muye. In those days, men possessed the full range of talents: when they went out as generals, they repelled enemies ten thousand li away; when they entered court as chief ministers, they discoursed on the Way within the palace hall. There was as yet no division between generals and chief ministers. After the Three Dynasties, civil and military functions began to diverge into two distinct paths.

Speaking of chief ministers, Shentu Jia wished to execute Chao Cuo, and Liu Quli wished to execute Tian Ren. Though they shared the desire to discharge the duties of a chief minister, Jia, with his forthright and loyal counsel, was worthier than Quli, who ultimately incurred execution. Chen Ping did not know the figures for judicial decisions, and Bing Ji did not inquire into deaths in a brawl. Though both understood the proper scope of a chief minister’s office, Ping’s illustrious founding services surpassed Ji’s lack of noteworthy proposals or achievements. Pei Du settled the strategy for pacifying Huai and Cai, and Li Deyu settled the strategy for pacifying Ze and Lu. Both rendered great service, but Du did not form a faction, whereas Deyu formed one to attack his opponents. Thus Du surpassed Deyu in virtue and magnanimity. Kongming served as chief minister to Zhaolie when the embers of the Han were being fanned back into flame, and Zhang Jun served as chief minister to Gaozong when the Song ruling house was being reestablished. Both displayed conspicuous loyalty, but Kongming could employ both Wei Yan and Yang Yi, whereas Jun could not employ both Qu Duan and Wu Jie. Thus Jun was inferior to Kongming in talent and capacity.

Speaking of generals, Deng Yu was enfeoffed as a marquis at twenty-four, and Xun Xian received the insignia of military command at twenty-eight. Both rendered meritorious service while young. Yet Yu was a founding worthy of the Eastern Han, whereas Xian’s achievements had not become distinguished…

title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
其成功之多寡可知矣謝玄以八千兵而
敗秦岳飛以五百騎而敗金皆以兵寡而
制衆也然飛以偏師獨克而玄以徼幸成
功其用兵之勝否可見矣李光弼斬張用
濟於軍門衛青不誅蘇建於境外其處事
雖異然光弼遭事之變而從權衛青當時
之平而守經各得其宜也馮奉世擅命以
誅莎車陳湯矯制以誅郅支其專命雖同
然莎車小國勝之未足威敵郅支勁虜誅
===
之足以安邊其功有間也夫隨陸無武遇
高帝而不能建封侯之業絳灌無文遇文
帝而不能興太平之治昔人嘗以為耻矣
求其出將入相文武唯其所用者亦未嘗
無人焉武侯表追伊傅而有興漢之功杜
預學專春秋而有平吳之績范仲淹儒臣
也宣撫陝右而元昊乞和虞允文儒臣也
督戰江上而女真敗走是皆才兼文武之
士也愚也鼓篋芹宫沐浴至教文事□□
punctuated:
其成功之多寡可知矣。謝玄以八千兵而敗秦，岳飛以五百騎而敗金，皆以兵寡而制衆也。然飛以偏師獨克，而玄以徼幸成功，其用兵之勝否可見矣。李光弼斬張用濟於軍門，衛青不誅蘇建於境外，其處事雖異，然光弼遭事之變而從權，衛青當時之平而守經，各得其宜也。馮奉世擅命以誅莎車，陳湯矯制以誅郅支，其專命雖同，然莎車小國，勝之未足威敵；郅支勁虜，誅之足以安邊，其功有間也。
夫隨陸無武，遇高帝而不能建封侯之業；絳灌無文，遇文帝而不能興太平之治。昔人嘗以為耻矣。求其出將入相、文武唯其所用者，亦未嘗無人焉。武侯表追伊傅，而有興漢之功；杜預學專《春秋》，而有平吳之績；范仲淹，儒臣也，宣撫陝右而元昊乞和；虞允文，儒臣也，督戰江上而女真敗走。是皆才兼文武之士也。愚也鼓篋芹宫，沐浴至教，文事□□
translation_en:
…the relative extent of their achievements can thus be understood. Xie Xuan defeated Qin with eight thousand soldiers, and Yue Fei defeated Jin with five hundred cavalrymen: both overcame larger forces with smaller ones. Yet Fei won independently with a detached force, whereas Xuan achieved success through good fortune. Their relative proficiency in warfare can thus be seen. Li Guangbi executed Zhang Yongji at the army’s gate, whereas Wei Qing did not execute Su Jian beyond the frontier. Although they handled affairs differently, Guangbi confronted exceptional circumstances and exercised discretion, while Wei Qing faced ordinary circumstances and adhered to established principles. Each acted appropriately. Feng Fengshi acted without authorization to punish Shache, and Chen Tang falsely invoked an imperial decree to kill Zhizhi. Although both assumed authority on their own initiative, Shache was a small state, and defeating it was insufficient to overawe the enemy; Zhizhi was a formidable barbarian foe, and killing him sufficed to secure the frontier. Their achievements differed in degree.
Sui He and Lu Jia lacked military abilities: although they served Emperor Gao, they could not perform deeds that earned enfeoffment as marquises. Jiang and Guan lacked civil accomplishments: although they served Emperor Wen, they could not bring about an era of great peace. People of earlier times regarded this as shameful. Yet there have certainly been men capable of serving as generals in the field and chief ministers at court, applying their civil or military talents as circumstances required. The Marquis of Wu, in his memorial, emulated Yi Yin and Fu Yue [?] and won distinction for reviving the Han. Du Yu specialized in the study of the Spring and Autumn Annals and achieved the pacification of Wu. Fan Zhongyan was a Confucian minister; when he served as Pacification Commissioner in Shanyou, Yuanhao sued for peace. Yu Yunwen was a Confucian minister; when he supervised the fighting on the Yangzi River, the Jurchens were defeated and fled. These were all men whose talents embraced both civil and military affairs. I, in my ignorance, have opened my book satchel to study in the school and have been bathed in the finest instruction. In literary matters, [two illegible characters]…

驚駕虬之句則知騷人之志高惟其潔故
常自疏濯汙淖之中惟其高故常欲浮游埃
壒之表彼賈生弔之揚雄反之未必知原
之志蘇子許之朱子註之斯為得原之心
執事發策以楚騷下詢承學殆亦憫原之
punctuated:
學，未能予奪品題，有志不職，惟執事恕其狂斐而教之，幸幸！
第肆問
陳典

Fourth Policy Question
Chen Dian
