title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
忠而惜其過感原之志而悲其不幸歟夫
原之在楚也以宗室之英為三閭之職序
其譜屬率其賢良以厲國士內則倚之為
蓍龜外則賴之為衡鑑夫何一沮於上官
之讒而懷王疏之再厄於子蘭之譖而襄
王放之薋菉盈室非幽蘭之可佩雄鳩鳴
逝而鳳鳥之𧹞當其登閬風而紲馬就重
華而陳辭亦豈得已哉故憂心煩亂而離
騷作焉述唐虞三后之制序桀紂羿澆之
===
敗以冀君之一悟而還己也不幸襄王終
不悟而九歌九章作焉彼太一之歌而繼
之以湘君或者譏其靡而不知九歌之作
皆以事神不答而不忘其敬此事君不合
而不忘其忠也何靡之有惜誦之章而繼
之以懷沙或者譏其矯而不知九章之作
皆忠愛之心發於嗟歎之餘憤懣之情形
於言意之表也何矯之有淮南王安曰國
風好色而不淫小雅怨誹而不亂離騷可
punctuated: 忠而惜其過，感原之志而悲其不幸歟？夫原之在楚也，以宗室之英為三閭之職，序其譜屬，率其賢良，以厲國士。內則倚之為蓍龜，外則賴之為衡鑑。夫何一沮於上官之讒，而懷王疏之；再厄於子蘭之譖，而襄王放之？薋菉盈室，非幽蘭之可佩；雄鳩鳴逝，而鳳鳥之𧹞。當其登閬風而紲馬，就重華而陳辭，亦豈得已哉？故憂心煩亂而《離騷》作焉，述唐虞三后之制，序桀紂羿澆之敗，以冀君之一悟而還己也。不幸襄王終不悟，而《九歌》《九章》作焉。彼《太一》之歌而繼之以《湘君》，或者譏其靡，而不知《九歌》之作，皆以事神不答而不忘其敬，此事君不合而不忘其忠也，何靡之有？《惜誦》之章而繼之以《懷沙》，或者譏其矯，而不知《九章》之作，皆忠愛之心發於嗟歎之餘，憤懣之情形於言意之表也，何矯之有？淮南王安曰：「《國風》好色而不淫，《小雅》怨誹而不亂，《離騷》可
translation_en: …his loyalty and regret his errors, feel moved by Qu Yuan’s aspirations and grieve over his misfortune? When Qu Yuan served in Chu, he was an outstanding member of the royal clan and held the office of Grand Master of the Three Clans. He put their genealogical affiliations in order and led their worthy and capable members, thereby encouraging the men of the state. Within the court, he was trusted like the divining stalks and tortoise shell; in external affairs, he was relied upon as a balance and mirror of judgment. How was it, then, that he was first thwarted by Shangguan’s slander, so that King Huai estranged himself from him, and then beset by Zilan’s calumnies, so that King Xiang banished him? With prickly weeds and green foxtail filling the chamber, there was no place for wearing the secluded orchid; the male dove cried as it flew, while the phoenix [?]. When he ascended Langfeng and tethered his horse, and approached Chonghua to present his words, could he have done otherwise? Thus, troubled and distraught at heart, he composed Encountering Sorrow (Li sao). He recounted the institutions of Tang and Yu and the Three Sovereigns, and set forth the downfalls of Jie, Zhou, Yi, and Jiao, hoping that his ruler might awaken to the truth and recall him. Unfortunately, King Xiang never understood, and so the Nine Songs (Jiu ge) and Nine Pieces (Jiu zhang) were composed. As for the song to Taiyi followed by that to the Lord of the Xiang River, some criticize their extravagance. They do not understand that throughout the Nine Songs, service to the spirits goes unanswered, yet reverence is never forgotten. This is service to a ruler without finding acceptance, yet never forgetting loyalty. What extravagance is there in that? As for the piece Lamenting My Recitation (Xi song), followed by Embracing Sand (Huai sha), some criticize their affectation. They do not understand that throughout the Nine Pieces, a heart full of loyalty and love finds expression in sighs and lamentation, while feelings of indignation and distress emerge beyond the words and their stated meaning. What affectation is there in that? An, Prince of Huainan, said: “The Airs of the States delight in beauty without licentiousness; the Lesser Odes voice resentment and criticism without disorder. Encountering Sorrow may…”

title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
謂兼之是知騷之為辭無愧於風雅矣宋
景文公曰離騷為詞賦之祖如至方不能
加矩至圓不能加規是知騷之為辭冠絕
乎古今矣賈誼弔原謂鳳凰翔于千仞覽
德輝而下之盖譏原之不去而不知原為
貴戚之臣不可以去也揚雄反騷謂臨江
瀕而掩涕何有九招與九歌盖譏騷之不
實而不知騷乃託興之語固非其實也若
夫招䰟作於宋玉極言上下四方之害而
===
陳楚國之樂即其辭而考之知其為招原
之辭夫豈誠原乎大招作於景差粗識屈
伸動靜之道國體時政之宜以大小言賦
驗之則知出於景差之手夫豈原詞乎招
隱之作則出於淮南之小山其辭最為高
古矣或因王孫不歸之辭而以為招原恐
未必然也成相之辭則出於蘭陵之荀况
其辭可為監戒矣今與佹詩六賦之辭同
載于荀子固非原徒也東坡以騷為風雅
punctuated: 謂兼之。」是知騷之為辭，無愧於風雅矣。宋景文公曰：「離騷為詞賦之祖，如至方不能加矩，至圓不能加規。」是知騷之為辭，冠絕乎古今矣。賈誼弔原，謂「鳳凰翔于千仞，覽德輝而下之」，盖譏原之不去，而不知原為貴戚之臣，不可以去也。揚雄反騷，謂「臨江瀕而掩涕，何有九招與九歌」，盖譏騷之不實，而不知騷乃託興之語，固非其實也。若夫招䰟作於宋玉，極言上下四方之害，而陳楚國之樂，即其辭而考之，知其為招原之辭，夫豈誠原乎？大招作於景差，粗識屈伸動靜之道、國體時政之宜，以大小言賦驗之，則知出於景差之手，夫豈原詞乎？招隱之作，則出於淮南之小山，其辭最為高古矣。或因王孫不歸之辭，而以為招原，恐未必然也。成相之辭，則出於蘭陵之荀况，其辭可為監戒矣。今與佹詩、六賦之辭，同載于荀子，固非原徒也。東坡以騷為風雅
translation_en:
…may be said to combine both.” From this we know that the language of Encountering Sorrow (Li sao) is worthy of the Airs and Odes. Lord Jingwen, Song Qi, said: “Encountering Sorrow is the ancestor of lyric compositions and rhapsodies: just as a carpenter’s square cannot improve perfect squareness, nor compasses perfect roundness.” From this we know that its language stands supreme throughout past and present.

In his lament for Qu Yuan, Jia Yi says, “The phoenix soars a thousand ren aloft; seeing the radiance of virtue, it descends.” He was apparently criticizing Qu Yuan for not leaving, without understanding that, as a minister related to the ruling house, Qu Yuan could not leave. In his Refutation of Encountering Sorrow (Fan sao), Yang Xiong says, “Standing at the river’s edge and wiping away tears—what use are the Nine Summons [?] and Nine Songs?” He was apparently criticizing Encountering Sorrow for its lack of factual truth, without understanding that its language conveys meaning through evocative imagery and was never intended as literal fact.

As for Summoning the Soul (Zhao hun), it was composed by Song Yu. It describes at length the dangers above and below and in all four directions, then sets forth the delights of the state of Chu. Examining its language shows that it is a summons addressed to Qu Yuan. How could it really be by Qu Yuan [?]? The Great Summons (Da zhao) was composed by Jing Cha. It displays a rudimentary understanding of the principles of withdrawal and advance, movement and repose, and of what is fitting for the organization of the state and the government of the day. Testing it against the Rhapsodies on Grand and Small Words shows that it came from Jing Cha’s hand. How could these be Qu Yuan’s words?

The Summons to the Recluse (Zhao yin) came from Xiaoshan of Huainan; its language is exceptionally lofty and antique. Some take its words about the noble scion who does not return as evidence that it summons Qu Yuan, but this may well be mistaken. The verses of Working Songs (Cheng xiang) came from Xun Kuang of Lanling and can serve as admonitions. They are now included in the Xunzi together with the Unusual Poem (Gui shi) and the Six Rhapsodies; their author certainly did not belong to Qu Yuan’s school. Dongpo regarded Encountering Sorrow as the Airs and Odes…

title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
再變而讀者謂得體蓋所學有得於騷也
温公不以騷編入通鑑而論者謂未純蓋
其例不取詩賦也豈可執是而輕議哉嗟
夫屈原之忠忠之過也屈原之過過乎中
也紫陽夫子有定論矣世之狃狃者豈足
以知原哉讀離騷者以周公鴟鴞之詩劉
向災異之疏合而觀之則知宗臣忠愛之
心矣愚也生長楚邦景仰先哲蓋嘗泛沅
江過湘水採江瀕之芳草弔魚腹之忠魂
===
未嘗不感慨太息想見其為人也茲承明
問欲悉陳之恐留更僕畧摭舊聞以對惟
進而教之幸甚
第五問
劉渙
同考試官教諭謝 批 此篇答者多敷演問目酌古準
今事全無斷制晚得此卷條答詳明識見超越且文采翩翩其獸中
之麟鳥中之鳳也有用之學非吾子而誰歸
考試官教諭孫 批 時務一策正欲觀諸士子學識
punctuated:
再變，而讀者謂得體，蓋所學有得於騷也。温公不以騷編入通鑑，而論者謂未純，蓋其例不取詩賦也，豈可執是而輕議哉！嗟夫！屈原之忠，忠之過也；屈原之過，過乎中也。紫陽夫子有定論矣。世之狃狃者，豈足以知原哉！讀離騷者，以周公鴟鴞之詩、劉向災異之疏合而觀之，則知宗臣忠愛之心矣。愚也生長楚邦，景仰先哲，蓋嘗泛沅江，過湘水，採江瀕之芳草，弔魚腹之忠魂，未嘗不感慨太息，想見其為人也。茲承明問，欲悉陳之，恐留更僕，畧摭舊聞以對，惟進而教之，幸甚。
第五問
劉渙
同考試官教諭謝批：此篇答者多敷演問目，酌古準今事全無斷制。晚得此卷，條答詳明，識見超越，且文采翩翩，其獸中之麟、鳥中之鳳也。有用之學，非吾子而誰歸？
考試官教諭孫批：時務一策，正欲觀諸士子學識。
translation_en:
…a second transformation, and readers judged that he had captured its proper character, for his learning had gained something from the Songs of Chu. Duke Wen, Sima Guang, did not include the Songs of Chu in the Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government, and critics judged this less than wholly satisfactory. Yet his editorial principles excluded poetry and rhapsodies: how could one seize upon this to criticize him lightly? Alas! Qu Yuan’s loyalty was loyalty carried to excess; Qu Yuan’s fault was to exceed the mean. Master Ziyang, Zhu Xi, has given a definitive judgment. How could the complacent and hidebound people of this world [?] be capable of understanding Qu Yuan? If readers consider Encountering Sorrow (Li sao) together with the Duke of Zhou’s poem The Owl and Liu Xiang’s memorials on calamities and anomalies, they will understand the loyal and loving heart of a minister of the ruling lineage. I, an unworthy man, was born and raised in Chu and revere its ancient worthies. I have sailed upon the Yuan River, passed along the Xiang River, gathered fragrant plants beside the rivers, and mourned the loyal soul in the bellies of fish. Never have I failed to sigh deeply with emotion and imagine the man he was. Now, receiving your discerning question, I would set everything forth, but fear detaining you through a change of attendants. I have therefore briefly gathered what I have previously learned in reply. I should count myself most fortunate if you would offer further instruction.
Fifth Question
Liu Huan
Comment by Associate Examiner Xie, Instructor: Most who answered this question merely elaborated its wording; in weighing antiquity against present circumstances, they offered no decisive judgments at all. Late in the process I obtained this script: its responses are detailed and clear, its insight outstanding, and its literary grace elegant. It is a qilin among beasts, a phoenix among birds. If learning of practical use does not belong to you, young man, to whom does it belong?
Comment by Examiner Sun, Instructor: The policy question on current affairs was intended precisely to reveal the candidates’ learning and understanding…

title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
此卷五策皆能敷答無齟齬而此篇稽古訂今尤條析詳整汪□□
洋譬猶孫吳制勝愈出愈竒而岷江厚源一瀉千里實學高識其我
湖湘之俊傑歟用世之才吾端於子是屬
考試官教諭李批答此策者多謂井田可復封建
可行禮樂之屬皆欲一二復古非通變之論也此作酌古準今鑿鑿可
行明體適用之學舎子其誰
善為治者不可不法乎古善法古者不可
不通乎今為治而不法古俗吏之見耳固
淺陋而不足法泥古而不通今迂儒之論
===
耳亦拘滯而不可行酌古之制而審今之
宜斯可以行之而無弊矣執事發策以時
務下詢承學盖待以俊傑也愚也不敏敢
不以俊傑自待乎天下之事多矣姑因明
問所及而陳之自溝洫甽澮之制壞於秦
而井田不可復矣彼師丹之限田李安世
之均田皆救弊之法也然均田之制不能
無弊必也用限田之法王侯之占田有限
庶人之授田有差則兼併之患塞豈不有
punctuated:
此卷五策皆能敷答，無齟齬，而此篇稽古訂今，尤條析詳整，汪□□洋，譬猶孫吳制勝，愈出愈竒，而岷江厚源，一瀉千里。實學高識，其我湖湘之俊傑歟！用世之才，吾端於子是屬。
考試官教諭李批：答此策者，多謂井田可復，封建可行，禮樂之屬皆欲一二復古，非通變之論也。此作酌古準今，鑿鑿可行。明體適用之學，舎子其誰！
善為治者，不可不法乎古；善法古者，不可不通乎今。為治而不法古，俗吏之見耳，固淺陋而不足法；泥古而不通今，迂儒之論耳，亦拘滯而不可行。酌古之制而審今之宜，斯可以行之而無弊矣。執事發策，以時務下詢承學，盖待以俊傑也。愚也不敏，敢不以俊傑自待乎？天下之事多矣，姑因明問所及而陳之。自溝洫甽澮之制壞於秦，而井田不可復矣。彼師丹之限田、李安世之均田，皆救弊之法也。然均田之制，不能無弊，必也用限田之法，王侯之占田有限，庶人之授田有差，則兼併之患塞，豈不有
translation_en:
…All five policy essays in this script develop their answers without inconsistencies. This essay in particular examines antiquity against present circumstances, analyzing its points with exceptional thoroughness and order. Its expansive flow [?] resembles Sun Wu and Wu Qi deploying winning strategies, each more remarkable than the last; it is also like the Min River, with its abundant headwaters, rushing a thousand li in a single torrent. With such substantial learning and lofty understanding, is he not an outstanding talent of our Huxiang region? As for talent capable of serving the world, I place my expectations squarely upon you.
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: Most who answered this policy question claimed that the well-field system could be restored and feudal enfeoffment put into practice. In matters such as rites and music, they wished to restore ancient practices item by item. These are not arguments that understand adaptation to changing circumstances. This essay weighs antiquity against the present, and its proposals are demonstrably practicable. In learning that illuminates fundamental principles and applies them appropriately, who but you can match it?
Those skilled in governing must take antiquity as their model; those skilled in taking antiquity as their model must understand the present. To govern without following antiquity is merely the outlook of a commonplace functionary: shallow and crude, it is certainly unworthy of emulation. To cling to antiquity without understanding the present is merely the argument of an impractical scholar: rigid and obstructive, it too cannot be put into practice. Only by weighing ancient institutions and examining what suits the present can one implement them without harmful consequences. You, honored examiners, have issued policy questions on current affairs to inquire of us students, evidently treating us as outstanding talents. Though I am dull and slow of understanding, dare I fail to hold myself to that standard? title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
近先王養民之良法乎侯伯子男之邦廢
於秦而封建不可行矣彼胡氏謂封建可
復范氏謂封建不可復是各有所見也然
胡氏之論高遠難行必也本范氏之說擇
人以任守令久任以責成功則龔黃之化
行豈不有得先王建邦之遺意乎虞夏商
周之禮不可得而見矣世之議禮者毎病
夫器數之難循欲制一代之禮必本朱子
儀禮經傳通解之書而叅以唐宋之典誠
===
祭必用簠豆而今之盤杆不廢也朝必以
弁冕而今之衣冠不革也則禮可制矣莖
英韶濩之樂不可得而聞矣世之論樂者
毎病夫音律之難審欲作一代之樂必用
蔡元定律呂新書之法而叅以唐宋之制
作截管候氣而聲氣之元可求也絫黍定
律而長短之度可驗也則樂可作矣兵寓
於農周制也居則為比閭族黨州鄉之民
行則為伍兩卒旅軍師之衆王安石保甲
punctuated: 近先王養民之良法乎？侯伯子男之邦廢於秦，而封建不可行矣。彼胡氏謂封建可復，范氏謂封建不可復，是各有所見也。然胡氏之論高遠難行，必也本范氏之說，擇人以任守令，久任以責成功，則龔黃之化行，豈不有得先王建邦之遺意乎？虞夏商周之禮不可得而見矣。世之議禮者毎病夫器數之難循。欲制一代之禮，必本朱子《儀禮經傳通解》之書，而叅以唐宋之典。誠祭必用簠豆，而今之盤杆不廢也；朝必以弁冕，而今之衣冠不革也，則禮可制矣。莖英韶濩之樂不可得而聞矣。世之論樂者毎病夫音律之難審。欲作一代之樂，必用蔡元定《律呂新書》之法，而叅以唐宋之制作。截管候氣，而聲氣之元可求也；絫黍定律，而長短之度可驗也，則樂可作矣。兵寓於農，周制也。居則為比閭族黨州鄉之民，行則為伍兩卒旅軍師之衆。王安石保甲
translation_en:
…approach the excellent methods by which the former kings nourished the people? The domains of marquises, earls, viscounts, and barons were abolished under the Qin, and enfeoffment can no longer be practiced. Master Hu maintained that enfeoffment could be restored, while Master Fan maintained that it could not; each had grounds for his view. Yet Master Hu’s argument is lofty and difficult to implement. We must instead follow Master Fan’s proposal: select suitable men to serve as prefects and magistrates, keep them in office for extended terms, and hold them responsible for achieving results. Then the transforming governance of Gong and Huang would prevail. Would this not recover something of the former kings’ original intent in establishing domains?

The rites of Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou can no longer be seen. Those who discuss ritual today repeatedly find it difficult to follow the prescribed vessels and numerical specifications. To establish the rites of a dynasty, we must take Master Zhu’s Comprehensive Explanation of the Classic and Commentaries on Ceremonial Ritual (Yili jingzhuan tongjie) as our foundation and supplement it with the institutions of the Tang and Song. If sacrifices duly employ the ritual grain vessels fu and dou, while present-day platters and other vessels [?] are not discarded, and court audiences duly employ ceremonial caps and crowns, while present-day robes and headgear are not abolished, then a system of rites can be established.

The music of Jing [?], Ying, Shao, and Huo can no longer be heard. Those who discuss music today repeatedly find it difficult to determine pitches and pitch standards accurately. To create the music of a dynasty, we must use the methods in Cai Yuanding’s New Book on Pitch Standards (Lü lü xinshu), supplemented by the arrangements of the Tang and Song. By cutting pitch pipes and observing the seasonal qi, the source of sound and qi can be sought; by piling up millet grains to establish pitch standards, the measurements of length can be verified. Thus music can be created.

Embedding soldiers among the farmers was the Zhou system. At home, they were the inhabitants organized into bi, lü, zu, dang, zhou, and xiang; on campaign, they were the troops organized into wu, liang, zu, lü, jun, and shi. Wang Anshi’s baojia system…

title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之法盖出於此然農務方殷有黙集之煩
期會稍稽有鞭笞之害是泥其法而不知
其意也必也用成周什伍之法使之三時
務農一時講武則民兵精銳而可以銷坐
食之費奚至於病民邪馬養於民古法也
平居則散之於民而閑牧之有法有事則
斂之於國而攻戰之有備王安石保馬之
法盖本於此然賦牧地於農民而斂其租
課散國馬於編戶而責其孳息是知其利
===
而不見其害也必也復成周車乘之制而
又寬其孳息之額嚴其隱盜之刑則牧馬
蕃息而可以給戎行之用豈至於厲衆邪
以文章取士非古也欲盡選材之法莫若
於文章之外兼察其德行每當開科之期
督學憲臣察其浮薄無行者詞華雖贍而
必黜奔競無耻者學問雖博而不容則凡
就試有司者皆經明行脩之士矣以資格
用人非古也欲盡官人之道莫若於資格
punctuated: 之法，盖出於此。然農務方殷，有黙集之煩；期會稍稽，有鞭笞之害。是泥其法而不知其意也。必也用成周什伍之法，使之三時務農，一時講武，則民兵精銳，而可以銷坐食之費，奚至於病民邪？馬養於民，古法也。平居則散之於民，而閑牧之有法；有事則斂之於國，而攻戰之有備。王安石保馬之法，盖本於此。然賦牧地於農民，而斂其租課；散國馬於編戶，而責其孳息。是知其利而不見其害也。必也復成周車乘之制，而又寬其孳息之額，嚴其隱盜之刑，則牧馬蕃息，而可以給戎行之用，豈至於厲衆邪？以文章取士，非古也。欲盡選材之法，莫若於文章之外兼察其德行。每當開科之期，督學憲臣察其浮薄無行者，詞華雖贍而必黜；奔競無耻者，學問雖博而不容。則凡就試有司者，皆經明行脩之士矣。以資格用人，非古也。欲盡官人之道，莫若於資格
translation_en:
…method presumably derived from this. Yet when farm work was at its busiest, there was the burden of mustering [?]; if men were even slightly late for an appointed assembly, they suffered flogging. This was to cling to the method without understanding its intent. One must employ the mature Zhou dynasty’s system of grouping households in tens and fives, having them farm for three seasons and practice warfare for one. Then the militia would be skilled and formidable, and the expense of feeding idle men could be eliminated. How could this become a burden upon the people?

Having the people rear horses was an ancient practice. In ordinary times, horses were distributed among the people, with proper methods for their training and pasturing; when military affairs arose, they were gathered by the state, so that preparations for combat were complete. Wang Anshi’s horse-maintenance system presumably had its basis in this. Yet he allotted pastureland to farmers while collecting rent and levies from it, and distributed state horses among registered households while demanding that they produce offspring. This was to recognize the benefits without seeing the harm. One must restore the mature Zhou dynasty’s system of chariot provision, relax the quotas for offspring, and impose strict penalties for concealing or stealing horses. Then the horses being reared would multiply and could supply the needs of the army. How could this become harmful to the people?

Selecting men through literary composition was not the ancient practice. To perfect the method of selecting talent, nothing is better than examining moral conduct as well as literary composition. Whenever an examination is held, the censorial officials supervising education should scrutinize the candidates: those who are frivolous and lack good conduct must be rejected, however rich their literary embellishments; those who shamelessly scramble for advancement must not be admitted, however extensive their learning. Then all who present themselves for examination before the responsible officials will be men who understand the Classics and cultivate their conduct.

Employing men according to prescribed qualifications and seniority was not the ancient practice. To perfect the way of appointing men to office, nothing is better than, beyond prescribed qualifications and seniority…

title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之外兼考其賢否每當選用之際典銓大
臣考其廉慎有為者資格未及而必升貪
庸不職者資格雖及而必殿則凡效官內
外者皆潔己奉公之人矣此數者皆當今
之要務也愚也學不足以博古才不足以
通今然幼而學之壯而欲行之亦情之不
能自已也執事恕其狂而進之教之幸甚
punctuated: 之外兼考其賢否。每當選用之際，典銓大臣考其廉慎有為者，資格未及而必升；貪庸不職者，資格雖及而必殿。則凡效官內外者，皆潔己奉公之人矣。此數者，皆當今之要務也。愚也，學不足以博古，才不足以通今，然幼而學之，壯而欲行之，亦情之不能自已也。執事恕其狂而進之、教之，幸甚！
translation_en:
…also assess their worthiness or unworthiness in addition to those qualifications. Whenever officials are selected for appointment, the high ministers responsible for personnel selection should examine them: those who are incorruptible, conscientious, and capable must be advanced even if they have not yet met the prescribed qualifications; those who are corrupt, mediocre, and neglectful of their duties must be placed last even if they have met those qualifications. Then all who serve in office, at court and in the provinces, will be people who maintain their personal integrity and devote themselves to public service.

These several matters are all urgent concerns of the present day. My learning is insufficient for a broad understanding of antiquity, and my ability insufficient for a thorough grasp of the present. Yet having studied these things in youth, I wish to put them into practice in adulthood: this, too, is a feeling I cannot restrain. If you, honored examiners, would pardon my presumption, advance me, and instruct me, I would be most fortunate!

title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
湖廣鄉試錄後序
成化十有六年時維大比湖
廣藩臬重臣協謀于巡按監
察御史楊謐聘昇等校文主
去取士昇等至合列郡暨戎
衛之士嚴試之定其可舉者
得八十五人故事有錄錄既
===
成謂昇宜序其後竊惟人才
致治之具也然人之才不一
上以是取則下以是進而治
之醇駁係焉虞周取士之法
稽諸經槩可見已自漢以來
有賢良方正之科有明經進
士之科有博學宏詞之科當
punctuated:
湖廣鄉試錄後序

成化十有六年，時維大比。湖廣藩臬重臣協謀于巡按監察御史楊謐，聘昇等校文，主去取士。昇等至，合列郡暨戎衛之士，嚴試之，定其可舉者，得八十五人。故事有錄，錄既成，謂昇宜序其後。

translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Huguang Provincial Examination

In the sixteenth year of Chenghua [1480], the time came for the triennial examination. The senior officials of Huguang’s Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions consulted with Yang Mi, the Regional Inspector serving as Investigating Censor, and invited me, Sheng, and my colleagues to evaluate the compositions and determine which candidates to accept or reject. Upon arriving, we assembled the candidates from the various prefectures and military guards, examined them rigorously, and selected eighty-five as qualified for recommendation. Established practice called for a record. Once it was completed, I was asked to write its postface.

I humbly consider talented men to be the means of achieving good government. Yet men’s talents differ. Whatever those above use as the criterion for selection becomes the means by which those below seek advancement; whether government is pure or mixed depends upon this. title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
是時士各以所長進不專於
經術故其措諸事業者亦有
醇有駁焉我
國家稽古立法盡罷諸科專以
明經取士其試之也四書五
經以驗其本領論詔誥表以
驗其詞藻判以觀其理事之
===
材策以觀其博古通今之學
盖兼明經宏詞之法以取士
也故士之進身者一本於經
術而措諸事業者粹然出於
正矣夫經以載道道以出治
明乎經然後明乎道明乎道
然後可推於治為我
punctuated: 是時，士各以所長進，不專於經術，故其措諸事業者亦有醇有駁焉。我國家稽古立法，盡罷諸科，專以明經取士。其試之也，四書、五經以驗其本領，論、詔、誥、表以驗其詞藻，判以觀其理事之材，策以觀其博古通今之學，盖兼明經、宏詞之法以取士也。故士之進身者一本於經術，而措諸事業者粹然出於正矣。夫經以載道，道以出治；明乎經，然後明乎道；明乎道，然後可推於治。為我
translation_en: … At that time, scholars advanced according to their particular strengths, without concentrating exclusively on classical learning. Consequently, their practical achievements also varied in purity and soundness. Our dynasty consulted antiquity in establishing its institutions, abolished all the various examination categories, and selected scholars solely for their understanding of the Classics. In examining them, it uses the Four Books and Five Classics to test their fundamental grounding; discourses, edicts, proclamations, and memorials to test their literary accomplishment; legal judgments to assess their ability to handle affairs; and policy essays to assess their breadth of learning about antiquity and understanding of the present. Thus, its selection of scholars combines the methods of the examinations in classical understanding and in literary composition. Accordingly, scholars seeking advancement base themselves entirely on classical learning, and what they put into practice in public affairs proceeds wholly from what is correct. The Classics convey the Way, and the Way gives rise to good government. title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
朝以明經取士盖以此也湖廣
古荆州之域北接雍豫南控
蠻獠東連吳粵西通巴蜀地
大而人衆衡山磅礴之氣九
嶷竒秀之精鍾為俊茂之材
而又遭遇
列聖以經術造之以科目□之
===
故百有餘年荆楚之士□□
經進者昭崇勛揚休烈卓然
為世名臣者不可稱數人才
治效之盛比隆虞周矣夫豈
漢唐宋可及哉諸士子登名
斯錄榮且幸矣行將羽儀
天朝以展其所學盍思自勉以求
punctuated: 朝以明經取士，盖以此也。湖廣，古荆州之域，北接雍豫，南控蠻獠，東連吳粵，西通巴蜀，地大而人衆。衡山磅礴之氣，九嶷竒秀之精，鍾為俊茂之材，而又遭遇列聖，以經術造之，以科目□之。故百有餘年，荆楚之士□□經進者，昭崇勛，揚休烈，卓然為世名臣者，不可稱數。人才治效之盛，比隆虞周矣，夫豈漢唐宋可及哉！諸士子登名斯錄，榮且幸矣！行將羽儀天朝，以展其所學，盍思自勉以求
translation_en: …this is why our dynasty selects men for office through their mastery of the Classics. Huguang occupies the territory of ancient Jingzhou. To the north it borders Yong and Yu; to the south it commands the Man and Liao peoples; to the east it adjoins Wu and Yue; and to the west it connects with Ba and Shu. Its territory is vast and its people numerous. The mighty vital force of Mount Heng and the wondrous, exquisite essence of the Jiuyi Mountains converge to produce men of outstanding talent. Moreover, they have had the good fortune to live under successive sage emperors, who have formed them through classical learning and [?] them through the examinations. Thus, for more than a hundred years, among the men of Jing and Chu who [?] advanced through classical learning, those who displayed great achievements, made illustrious their splendid deeds, and stood out as celebrated ministers of their age have been beyond counting. The abundance of talent and the excellence of government have rivaled the flourishing ages of Yu and Zhou. How could the Han, Tang, or Song equal them? title: 成化十六年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
其名乎能自勉焉異時覽斯
錄者將指其名曰是忠肅以
事上者是惠和以保民者是
恭儉以禔身者則豈惟斯
之光昇等亦與有
施施焉衎衎焉巧言
播其惡焉人將指其
===
毀信廢忠者是服讒
是侵欲崇侈者則豈
之玷昇等亦與有
可不懼哉可不戒哉
直隸松江府上海縣儒學教
諭孫昇謹序
punctuated:
其名乎？能自勉焉，異時覽斯錄者，將指其名曰：「是忠肅以事上者，是惠和以保民者，是恭儉以禔身者。」則豈惟斯之光，昇等亦與有。施施焉，衎衎焉，巧言播其惡焉，人將指其毀信廢忠者，是服讒，是侵欲崇侈者，則豈之玷，昇等亦與有。可不懼哉？可不戒哉？
直隸松江府上海縣儒學教諭孫昇謹序。
translation_en:
…their reputation? If they can exert themselves, those who read this record in years to come will point to their names and say: “This one served his superiors loyally and reverently; this one protected the people with kindness and harmony; this one maintained his own conduct with respectfulness and frugality.” Then would the glory belong only to this [record?]? I, Sheng, and my colleagues would also share in it [?]. Self-satisfied and cheerful, with glib words spreading their wickedness [?], people will point to those who destroy trust and abandon loyalty, those who heed slander, and those who pursue grasping desires and exalt extravagance [?]. Then would the disgrace fall only upon [this record?]? I, Sheng, and my colleagues would also share in it [?]. Can we fail to fear this? Can we fail to take warning?
Respectfully prefaced by Sun Sheng, Instructor of the Confucian School of Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered territory.
